title: [Assembler] Identity pto.tmov (dst == src) causes spurious sync insertion, hanging on A5
body:
When a `pto.tmov` instruction has the same source and destination (identity move), ptoas still treats it as a data-movement op and inserts sync instructions around it. These spurious syncs cause synchronization errors that hang the kernel on A5. The same code passes on A3 due to different sync behavior between the two platforms.

## Root Cause

ptoas unconditionally inserts sync instructions around every `pto.tmov`. When the tmov is a no-op (dst == src), the syncs are unnecessary and harmful.

## Suggested Fix

ptoas should detect identity `pto.tmov` instructions (where source and destination resolve to the same address/MemRef) and either:
1. Skip sync insertion for identity moves, or
2. Eliminate identity `pto.tmov` instructions entirely

## Reproducer

[fa5_softmax_rescale.py](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/26403743/fa5_softmax_rescale.py)

## Related

- hw-native-sys/pypto#828 (original issue, filed on wrong repo)
- hw-native-sys/pypto#803
- hw-native-sys/pypto-lib#58

## Note

A complementary fix has been applied on the pypto side (hw-native-sys/pypto#836) to avoid emitting identity `pto.tmov` in the first place. However, ptoas should still handle this case defensively.

title: [Feature] pto.tmrgsort format2 should support 2-way and 3-way merge (currently hardcoded to 4-way)
body:
## Background

`pto.tmrgsort` currently has two formats:

- **format1**: single-list intra-block merge, `ins(src, blockLen)`
- **format2**: multi-list merge, **hardcoded to exactly 4 sources**, `ins(src0, src1, src2, src3)`

However, the underlying PTO-ISA `TMRGSORT` instruction supports 2-way, 3-way, and 4-way merges:

```
// 2-way
TMRGSORT(dst, executedNumList, tmp, src0, src1)
// 3-way
TMRGSORT(dst, executedNumList, tmp, src0, src1, src2)
// 4-way (currently supported)
TMRGSORT(dst, executedNumList, tmp, src0, src1, src2, src3)
```

## Current Limitation

`isFormat2()` hardcodes a 4-source requirement (`include/PTO/IR/PTOOps.td:3246`):

```cpp
bool isFormat2() { return getSrcs().size() == 4u && getDsts().size() == 2u && getExcuted(); }
```

The `print` function also hardcodes access to exactly 4 srcs (`lib/PTO/IR/PTO.cpp:4521-4524`).

Passing 2 or 3 sources triggers the catch-all verifier error:

```
tmrgsort expects format1 (1 src + blockLen + 1 dst) or format2 (4 srcs, outs dst, excuted)
```

## Expected Behavior

format2 should accept 2, 3, or 4 sources. The `isFormat2()` predicate should be relaxed to `srcs.size() >= 2 && srcs.size() <= 4`.

Assembly format would become variadic:

```mlir
// 2-way
pto.tmrgsort ins(%src0, %src1 {exhausted = false} : ...) outs(%dst, %tmp, %excuted : ...)

// 3-way
pto.tmrgsort ins(%src0, %src1, %src2 {exhausted = false} : ...) outs(%dst, %tmp, %excuted : ...)
```

## Layers Requiring Changes

- [ ] `include/PTO/IR/PTOOps.td` — relax `isFormat2()` predicate
- [ ] `lib/PTO/IR/PTO.cpp` — update `print`, `parse`, and `verify` to handle variable-length srcs
- [ ] `lib/PTO/Transforms/PTOViewToMemref.cpp` — update lowering patterns for variable-length srcs
- [ ] `docs/PTO_IR_manual.md` — update format2 assembly format description and examples
- [ ] `test/` — add regression tests for 2-way and 3-way cases

title: [Bug] generated C++ Cube kernel hangs with version >= 0.18
body:
### Component
EmitC / Codegen (lib/PTO/Transforms/PTOToEmitC.cpp)

### Description
The generated C++ in versions >= 0.18 appears to preserve the same overall math,
tensor views, and tensor layout for this kernel, but it changes the pipeline event
synchronization (`set_flag` / `wait_flag`) and tail synchronization behavior.

The version generated by 0.17 works for this reproducer. In that working output,
the event sequence is initialized before entering the loops, and the kernel ends
with explicit waits that drain the outstanding event dependencies.

In the >= 0.18 output, the synchronization schedule is different. In the failing
variant, the first main loop begins with:

  wait_flag(PIPE_M, PIPE_MTE1, EVENT_ID2);
  wait_flag(PIPE_M, PIPE_MTE1, EVENT_ID3);

but there is no obvious pre-loop:

  set_flag(PIPE_M, PIPE_MTE1, EVENT_ID3);

before that first wait on `EVENT_ID3`.

I compared the MLIR from the older working version and the newer failing version,
and for this kernel they appear identical in substance. The generated C++ differs
mainly in synchronization/event scheduling, which suggests the regression is
introduced downstream during EmitC/codegen or sync insertion rather than in the

The old working version did not have this issue and used a fully initialized and
explicitly drained event schedule.

This appears to cause invalid synchronization behavior in the generated kernel,
potentially resulting in:
- hang / deadlock
- dependence on stale event state
- nondeterministic execution

Tail behavior also changed.

Old working version ended with:

  pipe_barrier(PIPE_ALL);
  wait_flag(PIPE_M, PIPE_MTE1, EVENT_ID2);
  wait_flag(PIPE_FIX, PIPE_M, EVENT_ID2);
  wait_flag(PIPE_M, PIPE_MTE1, EVENT_ID7);
  wait_flag(PIPE_FIX, PIPE_M, EVENT_ID6);

The failing generated version instead ends with:

  ptoas_auto_sync_tail(PTOAutoSyncTailMode::kBarrierAll);

which lowers to a barrier-only path and no longer explicitly drains those event
dependencies in the same way.

title: A5 target hangs on RMSNorm vector kernel that passes on A2A3
body:
## Problem

A PTO-IR vector kernel (`decode_projection_incore_0.pto`) compiles and runs correctly when targeting **A2A3**, but **hangs at runtime** when compiled for **A5**.

## Environment

- **PTOAS version**: 0.22

## Reproduction

PTO file attached below.

[decode_projection_incore_0.pto.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/26457179/decode_projection_incore_0.pto.txt)
[rmsnorm_incore_0.pto.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/26457180/rmsnorm_incore_0.pto.txt)

Steps:
1. Change `pto.target_arch` from `"a2a3"` to `"a5"` in the module attributes
2. Compile with `ptoas`
3. Run on A5 platform — program **hangs indefinitely** (no crash, no error)

## Behavior

| Target | Compile | Run |
|--------|---------|-----|
| A2A3 | OK | OK |
| A5 | OK | **Hangs** |

## Kernel Summary

This is a **RMSNorm vector kernel** (`decode_projection_incore_0`) from the Qwen3-32B decode layer projection. It operates on `[16, 5120]` BF16 input with `K_CHUNK=128` (40 iterations):

1. **Loop 1** — accumulate squared partial sums: `tload` → `tcvt`(bf16→f32) → `tmul`(x²) → `trowsum` → `tadd` (accumulate) → `tmov`
2. **Post-loop** — compute inv_rms: `tmuls`(÷5120) → `tadds`(+ε) → `trsqrt`
3. **Loop 2** — apply normalization: `tload` → `tcvt` → `trowexpandmul`(×inv_rms) → `tcolexpandmul`(×γ) → `tcvt`(f32→bf16) → `tstore`

## Operations Used

`tload`, `tstore`, `tcvt`, `tmul`, `trowsum`, `tadd`, `tmov`, `tmuls`, `tadds`, `trsqrt`, `trowexpandmul`, `tcolexpandmul`, `texpands`

## PTO File

<!-- Please attach the .pto file here -->

## Context

Discovered during E2E validation of `pypto-lib` Qwen3-32B decode tilelet (hw-native-sys/pypto-lib#58, Scope 1).

### Component
Passes / Transforms (sync insertion via `--enable-insert-sync`)

### Description
There appears to be a regression in sync instruction insertion triggered by `--enable-insert-sync`.

For the same input file:

- PTOAS `v0.17` works
- PTOAS `v0.22` hangs indefinitely

The reporter can attach the exact `.pto` file after the issue is created.

### Reproduction (minimal)
Run PTOAS with sync insertion enabled on the same input file:

```bash
ptoas build_output/GemmProgram_20260407_154637/ptoas/gemm_incore_0.pto \
  -o build_output/GemmProgram_20260407_154637/ptoas/gemm_incore_0.cpp \
  --enable-insert-sync \
  --pto-level=level3
```

Observed behavior:

1. PTOAS `v0.17` completes successfully
2. PTOAS `v0.22` hangs indefinitely on the same input

Current file path in the reporter workspace:

[gemm_incore_0.pto.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/26531266/gemm_incore_0.pto.txt)

The reporter can attach this file to the issue after creation.

### Expected behavior
`v0.22` should handle this input the same way as `v0.17`, or fail with a diagnostic. It should not hang.

### Actual behavior / error logs
With `--enable-insert-sync`, `v0.22` gets stuck on this input and does not finish. No useful diagnostic has been captured yet.

title: [Bug] WidenEventId places loop 2's wait_flag outside the loop instead of inside it
body:
### Component

EmitC / Codegen (lib/PTO/Transforms/PTOToEmitC.cpp)

### Description

The fix in PR #443 (commit 7198be3) works correctly when a function has a single loop, but breaks when two independent loops exist in the same function. Because both loops use the same pipe pair, PTOAS sees that the pipe pair is already claimed by loop 1 and skips setting up proper guards for loop 2. The result: the set and wait are both placed outside the loop and immediately cancel each other out, leaving the loop body running with no synchronization at all.

### Reproduction (minimal)

The zip contains three files compiled from the same input: the working 0.09 output, the broken 0.24 output, and a hand-corrected working 0.24 version.

In 0.24, a wait instruction for the second loop is placed outside the loop and immediately consumed before entering the loop, so the loop never actually waits. The fix moves it inside the loop where it should belong. See the diff:

```bash
$ diff inverse_0_24.cpp inverse_0_24_fixed.cpp 
185d184
<   wait_flag(PIPE_M, PIPE_MTE1, EVENT_ID7);
187a187
>     wait_flag(PIPE_M, PIPE_MTE1, EVENT_ID7);
215a216
>     set_flag(PIPE_M, PIPE_MTE1, EVENT_ID7);
261a263
>   wait_flag(PIPE_M, PIPE_MTE1, EVENT_ID7);
```

### Expected behavior

`set_flag(PIPE_M, PIPE_MTE1, EVENT_IDx)` is emitted immediately before each loop starts, and the matching wait_flag is placed as the first instruction inside the loop body, so each iteration waits for the previous one's signal before proceeding.

### Actual behavior / error logs

`set_flag(PIPE_M, PIPE_MTE1, EVENT_ID7)` is correctly placed immediately before loop 2, but the matching wait_flag is placed right after it — also outside the loop. The two instructions cancel each other out immediately, and the loop body runs with no synchronization guard at all.

title: [Feature] 支持 fillpad_inplace 基于同地址判断
body:
### Summary

目前 PTOAS 在 lowering pto.tfillpad 时，如果判断 src == dst，就会直接选择生成 TFILLPAD_INPLACE。但从 ISA 侧实现来看，FILLPAD_INPLACE 在运行时会同时读取src.GetValidRow()/GetValidCol()、dst.GetValidRow()/GetValidCol()，这意味着它实际上依赖的是src 提供原始有效区边界，dst 提供目标填充范围边界。TFILLPAD_INPLACE 的合理语义不应简单理解为“同一个 tile value 的 fillpad”，而应理解为：
      1.src 和 dst 指向同一块底层地址
      2.原地 padding
而当前的ptoas语义， src 和 dst 是同一个 tile 对象，它们的 validshape 通常相同，pto.tfillpad(tileA, tileA)转换成底层cce表达TFILLPAD_INPLACE（tileA, tileA)，实际运行并没有执行任何填充操作。

### Motivation / use case

a5功能

### Proposed API / behavior

是否可以改为根据src或者dst同地址进行判断，或者显示支持pto.tfillpad_inplace

### Alternatives considered

_No response_

title: [Bug] --pto-arch=a5 may mis-verify pto.tsel(i8) as A2/A3 during parse-time verifier
body:
### Component

PTO IR verifier / parser arch dispatch

### Description

When compiling textual `.pto` without module-level `pto.target_arch`, using `--pto-arch=a5` can still mis-verify `pto.tsel(i8)` as A2/A3 during parse-time verification:

`'pto.tsel' op expects A2/A3 tsel src0, src1, and dst element type to be i16/i32/f16/f32`

A5 is expected to accept i8 for `pto.tsel`.

I built a minimal reproducer with 2 `func.func` ops, each containing only `alloc_tile + pto.tsel(i8)`.

### Reproduction (minimal)

Reproducer file:

`test/repro/issue_tls_arch_tsel_i8_min.pto`

Command:

`build/tools/ptoas/ptoas --pto-arch=a5 test/repro/issue_tls_arch_tsel_i8_min.pto -o -`

### Expected behavior

`pto.tsel(i8)` should pass verifier on A5.

### Actual behavior / error logs

```text
loc("test/repro/issue_tls_arch_tsel_i8_min.pto":21:5): error: 'pto.tsel' op expects A2/A3 tsel src0, src1, and dst element type to be i16/i32/f16/f32
loc("test/repro/issue_tls_arch_tsel_i8_min.pto":34:5): error: 'pto.tsel' op expects A2/A3 tsel src0, src1, and dst element type to be i16/i32/f16/f32
Error: Failed to parse MLIR.
```

### Control experiment

If I add module attr explicitly:

`module attributes {"pto.target_arch" = "a5"} { ... }`

Then run:

`build/tools/ptoas/ptoas test/repro/issue_tls_arch_tsel_i8_min_attr.pto -o -`

the `A2/A3 tsel` verifier error disappears.

### Suspected root cause

`getVerifierTargetArch()` falls back to `getPTOParserTargetArch()` when module attr is not yet visible.

`getPTOParserTargetArch()` uses thread-local storage. MLIR parser verifies immediately after parse (`verifyAfterParse=true`) and verifier parallelizes `IsolatedFromAbove` children. Since `func.func` is `IsolatedFromAbove`, some op verifiers run on worker threads and may read default TLS arch (Unspecified/A3), causing wrong A2/A3 dispatch.

### Environment

- Repo: `hw-native-sys/PTOAS`
- Local branch: feature-vpto-backend
- Local commit: f4c679ae9916d586211199adf42025977f574f9e
- Tool: gh version 2.45.0 (2025-07-18 Ubuntu 2.45.0-1ubuntu0.3)

title: [Feature] Support multiple cross-core pipes per Cube/Vector function
body:
### Summary

  Could PTOAS support more than one cross-core pipe per Cube/Vector function?

  In our mixed-kernel flow, an AIC/AIV function pair may need bidirectional communication. Today this appears to be modeled as a single frontend `initialize_pipe` per function,
  and when both directions are needed it lowers to one `DIR_BOTH` pipe. As a result, the available pipe capacity is effectively shared by C2V and V2C instead of having two
  independent directional pipes.

### Motivation / use case

  After mixed-kernel splitting in PyPTO, we may end up with both of these directions in the same Cube/Vector function pair:

  - AIC -> AIV transfers (`tpush_to_aiv` / `tpop_from_aic`)
  - AIV -> AIC transfers (`tpush_to_aic` / `tpop_from_aiv`)

  The current restriction seems to be that each Cube/Vector kernel can only have at most one pipe init. So if both directions are present, we have to use one bidirectional pipe
  and split its capacity between the two directions.

  What we would ideally like instead is:

  - one C2V pipe for AIC -> AIV
  - one V2C pipe for AIV -> AIC

  That would avoid the current "one pipe shared by both directions" limitation.

### Proposed API / behavior

  Ideally, PTOAS could allow multiple frontend pipe instances for the same function pair, for example two separate pipes in a bidirectional case:

  ```mlir
  // Cube side
  pto.aic_initialize_pipe {dir_mask = 1, slot_size = ...} (...)
  pto.aic_initialize_pipe {dir_mask = 2, slot_size = ...} (...)

  // Vector side
  pto.aiv_initialize_pipe {dir_mask = 1, slot_size = ...} (...)
  pto.aiv_initialize_pipe {dir_mask = 2, slot_size = ...} (...)
  ```

  I realize this likely requires some way for tpush / tpop / tfree ops to identify which pipe they belong to, because the current frontend transfer ops do not carry an explicit
  pipe handle.

  If supporting multiple pipes is not the intended direction, could you clarify whether the limitation comes from:

  - the current PTOAS frontend IR / lowering design,
  - pto-isa,
  - or a lower-level software / hardware constraint?

### Alternatives considered

  The current workaround is to use a single `dir_mask = 3` pipe for both directions. This is functionally workable, but it forces C2V and V2C to share one pipe instead of using two
  independent directional pipes.

### Additional context

  From reading the current PTOAS design and lowering code, my understanding is:

  - frontend tpush / tpop / tfree ops do not carry a pipe operand / handle,
  - PTOAS currently enforces at most one `pto.aic_initialize_pipe` or `pto.aiv_initialize_pipe` per function,
  - when `dir_mask = 3`, both frontend directions are bound to the same internal `DIR_BOTH` pipe.

  So the main question is whether this is only a current frontend/lowering design choice, or whether there is some deeper reason that makes multiple pipes per Cube/Vector
  function impossible or undesirable.

title: [Feature] Support interleaved tpop/tfree schedules on a single pipe
body:
### Summary

  Could PTOAS support interleaved consumer schedules for `tpop` / `tfree` on the same pipe, instead of requiring the current strict pattern:

  `tpop -> use -> tfree -> next tpop`

  What we would like to enable is a double-buffered style schedule where a consumer can prefetch the next tile before the current tile is freed, so that `tpop` and `use` have a chance to overlap.

### Motivation / use case

  In our mixed-kernel flow, the consumer side of a cross-core pipe is currently forced into a serialized pattern:

  1. `tpop` one tile
  2. use that tile
  3. `tfree`
  4. only then issue the next `tpop`

  This prevents interleaved schedules such as:

  ```mlir
  %t0 = pto.tpop(%tile0, %pipe) {split = 0}
  %t1 = pto.tpop(%tile1, %pipe) {split = 0}

  use(%t0)
  use(%t1)

  pto.tfree(%pipe) {split = 0}
  pto.tfree(%pipe) {split = 0}

  or loop-pipelined forms like:

  %curr = pto.tpop(%tile0, %pipe) {split = 0}
  scf.for ... {
    %next = pto.tpop(%tile1, %pipe) {split = 0}   // prefetch next tile
    use(%curr)
    pto.tfree(%pipe) {split = 0}
    %curr = %next
  }
  ```

  Supporting this kind of schedule would make double buffering possible on the consumer side, and may expose overlap / latency-hiding opportunities between tpop and compute.

### Proposed API / behavior

  At a minimum, it would be useful to support more than one outstanding tpop on the same pipe, as long as the frees are still explicit and balanced.

  However, from reading the current PTOAS IR and passes, it looks like the main limitation is that pto.tfree only carries pipe_handle, not the identity of the borrowed tile / slot. So if interleaved schedules are to be supported, PTOAS may need one of these directions:

  - make tfree target a specific borrowed tile or pop token, instead of only a pipe handle
  - introduce an explicit borrow / token result from tpop
  - or use some other internal representation that can distinguish multiple outstanding consumer slots on the same pipe

### Alternatives considered

  The current workaround is to keep the strict serialized pattern:

  tpop -> use -> tfree -> next tpop

  This is functionally correct, but it prevents consumer-side double buffering and any possible overlap between prefetching the next tile and using the current tile.

### Additional context

  From the current PTOAS code, this restriction appears to be intentional today:

  - PTOVerifyTFree rejects: multiple outstanding pops on the same pipe are not supported
  - pto.tfree is defined as releasing the current consumer slot for a pipe, and it only takes pipe_handle
  - frontend tfree_from_aic / tfree_from_aiv also lower to pto.tfree(%pipe) without carrying tile identity

  So the main question is:

  Is it feasible to support interleaved / double-buffered tpop consumer schedules in PTOAS, or is there a deeper constraint in EmitC / pto-isa / lower-level software or hardware that fundamentally requires only one outstanding consumer pop per pipe?

title: [Bug] addptr lowering bug
body:
### Component

PTO Dialect / ODS (include/PTO/IR)

### Description

#486 seems to have a problem causing core dump in llvm.

### Reproduction (minimal)

```mlir
module {
  func.func @cube_kernel(%arg0: !pto.ptr<f32>, %arg1: !pto.ptr<f32>, %arg2: !pto.ptr<f32>) attributes {pto.kernel_kind = #pto.kernel_kind<cube>} {
    %c0 = arith.constant 0 : index
    %c1 = arith.constant 1 : index
    %c16 = arith.constant 16 : index
    %c2048 = arith.constant 2048 : index
    %0 = pto.get_block_idx
    %1 = arith.index_cast %0 : i64 to index
    %2 = arith.muli %1, %c2048 : index

    // THIS IS THE PROBLEM ####
    // Without this addptr it compiles if we just use %arg0
    %3 = pto.addptr %arg0, %2 : <f32> -> <f32>
    %4 = pto.import_reserved_buffer{name = "c2v_fifo", peer_func = @vector_kernel} -> i32
    %5 = pto.reserve_buffer{name = "v2c_fifo", size = 4096, location = <mat>, auto = true} -> i32
    pto.aic_initialize_pipe{dir_mask = 3, slot_size = 1024} (gm_slot_buffer = %3 : !pto.ptr<f32>, c2v_consumer_buf = %4 : i32, v2c_consumer_buf = %5 : i32)
    return
  }
  func.func @vector_kernel(%arg0: !pto.ptr<f32>) attributes {pto.kernel_kind = #pto.kernel_kind<vector>} {
    %c2048 = arith.constant 2048 : index
    %0 = pto.get_block_idx
    %1 = arith.index_cast %0 : i64 to index
    %2 = arith.muli %1, %c2048 : index
//    %3 = pto.addptr %arg0, %2 : <f32> -> <f32>
    %4 = pto.reserve_buffer{name = "c2v_fifo", size = 4096, location = <vec>, auto = true} -> i32
    %5 = pto.import_reserved_buffer{name = "v2c_fifo", peer_func = @cube_kernel} -> i32
    pto.aiv_initialize_pipe{dir_mask = 3, slot_size = 1024} (gm_slot_buffer = %arg0 : !pto.ptr<f32>, c2v_consumer_buf = %4 : i32, v2c_consumer_buf = %5 : i32)
    return
  }
  func.func @call_both(%arg0: memref<256xi64>, %arg1: !pto.ptr<f32>, %arg2: !pto.ptr<f32>, %arg3: !pto.ptr<f32>) attributes {pto.entry} {
    pto.set_ffts %arg0 : memref<256xi64>
    call @cube_kernel(%arg1, %arg2, %arg3) : (!pto.ptr<f32>, !pto.ptr<f32>, !pto.ptr<f32>) -> ()
    call @vector_kernel(%arg1) : (!pto.ptr<f32>) -> ()
    return
  }
}
```

### Expected behavior

generate the correct pointer arithmetic for the gm_slot_buffer in cube_kernel.



### Actual behavior / error logs

```text
ptoas: /llvm-workspace/llvm-project/llvm/include/llvm/Support/Casting.h:566: decltype(auto) llvm::cast(const From&) [with To = mlir::detail::TypedValue<mlir::pto::PtrType>; From = mlir::Value]: Assertion `isa<To>(Val) && "cast<Ty>() argument of incompatible type!"' failed.
Aborted (core dumped)
```

To reproduce, the generated cpp requires some manual fixes. See the perl lines in this shell script:

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
ARTIFACT_DIR="${SCRIPT_DIR}/build_artifacts"
MLIR_PATH="${ARTIFACT_DIR}/fa_gen.mlir"
GENERATED_CPP="${ARTIFACT_DIR}/fa_gen.cpp"
LIB_PATH="${ARTIFACT_DIR}/fa_lib.so"

PTO_LIB_PATH="${PTO_LIB_PATH:-/sources/pto-isa}"

mkdir -p "${ARTIFACT_DIR}"
rm -f "${GENERATED_CPP}" "${LIB_PATH}"

python "${SCRIPT_DIR}/kernels/fa_builder.py" > "${MLIR_PATH}"
# No --enable-insert-sync: the DSL builder inserts explicit sync primitives.
ptoas --pto-arch=a3 --enable-insert-sync "${MLIR_PATH}" > "${GENERATED_CPP}"

# Per-block GM-slot partitioning: TPipe does NOT offset the GM slot buffer by
# block_idx.  All blocks would share the same 8 GM slots, corrupting each
# other's c2v/v2c data.  We inject an offset into call_both so that each block
# gets its own 8-slot region.
#
# Offset = SLOTS_PER_BLOCK * SLOT_SIZE / sizeof(float)
#        = 8 * (S0 * max(S1_TILE, HEAD) * 4) / 4
#        = 8 * S0 * max(S1_TILE, HEAD)
#        = 8 * 32 * 256 = 65536  fp32 elements
GM_ELEMS_PER_BLOCK=$(python3 -c "
S0, HEAD, S1_TILE, SLOTS_PER_BLOCK = 32, 32, 256, 8
print(SLOTS_PER_BLOCK * S0 * max(S1_TILE, HEAD))
")
perl -pi -e "s/  cube_kernel\\(v2,/  __gm__ float* gm_per_blk = v2 + get_block_idx() * ${GM_ELEMS_PER_BLOCK};\\n  cube_kernel(gm_per_blk,/" "${GENERATED_CPP}"
perl -pi -e "s/  vector_kernel\\(v2,/  vector_kernel(gm_per_blk,/" "${GENERATED_CPP}"

bisheng \
    -I"${PTO_LIB_PATH}/include" \
    -fPIC -shared -D_FORTIFY_SOURCE=2 -O2 -std=c++17 \
    -Wno-macro-redefined -Wno-ignored-attributes -fstack-protector-strong \
    -xcce -Xhost-start -Xhost-end \
    -mllvm -cce-aicore-stack-size=0x8000 \
    -mllvm -cce-aicore-function-stack-size=0x8000 \
    -mllvm -cce-aicore-record-overflow=true \
    -mllvm -cce-aicore-addr-transform \
    -mllvm -cce-aicore-dcci-insert-for-scalar=false \
    --npu-arch=dav-2201 -DMEMORY_BASE \
    -std=gnu++17 \
    -DKERNEL_CPP="\"${GENERATED_CPP}\"" \
    "${SCRIPT_DIR}/caller.cpp" \
    -o "${LIB_PATH}"

echo "Generated ${GENERATED_CPP}."
echo "Built ${LIB_PATH}."
```

These two lines are currently needed for a bug in addptr, see #497 
```bash
perl -pi -e "s/  cube_kernel\\(v2,/  __gm__ float* gm_per_blk = v2 + get_block_idx() * ${GM_ELEMS_PER_BLOCK};\\n  cube_kernel(gm_per_blk,/" "${GENERATED_CPP}"
perl -pi -e "s/  vector_kernel\\(v2,/  vector_kernel(gm_per_blk,/" "${GENERATED_CPP}"
```

### Expected behavior

the generated kernel should use all 48 vector cores on A3

### Actual behavior / error logs

No errors to show, the generated kernel matches the torch npu fused attention reference, but it is way slower:

title: [Bug] pto.tdivs scalar-first syntax loses direction in mainline (ins(%scalar, %src) normalized)
body:
### Component

PTO Dialect / `TDivSOp` parser + canonical operand handling (`lib/PTO/IR/PTO.cpp`)

### Description

`pto.tdivs` loses operand direction semantics for textual form `ins(%scalar, %src)`.

Both forms:
- `ins(%src, %scalar)`
- `ins(%scalar, %src)`

are normalized to the same internal operand order `(tile, scalar, dst)`, so `scalar / src` cannot be represented.

### Minimal reproduction (mainline, no VPTO flags)

Input file: `test/dsl/issue_117_repro.pto`

```mlir
module {
  func.func @TDIVS_SRC_SCALAR() {
    %a = pto.alloc_tile : !pto.tile_buf<loc=vec, dtype=f32, rows=16, cols=64, v_row=16, v_col=64,
                                        blayout=row_major, slayout=none_box, fractal=512, pad=0>
    %dst = pto.alloc_tile : !pto.tile_buf<loc=vec, dtype=f32, rows=16, cols=64, v_row=16, v_col=64,
                                          blayout=row_major, slayout=none_box, fractal=512, pad=0>
    %scalar = arith.constant 2.0 : f32
    pto.tdivs ins(%a, %scalar : !pto.tile_buf<loc=vec, dtype=f32, rows=16, cols=64, v_row=16, v_col=64,
                               blayout=row_major, slayout=none_box, fractal=512, pad=0>, f32)
              outs(%dst : !pto.tile_buf<loc=vec, dtype=f32, rows=16, cols=64, v_row=16, v_col=64,
                                        blayout=row_major, slayout=none_box, fractal=512, pad=0>)
    return
  }

  func.func @TDIVS_SCALAR_SRC() {
    %a = pto.alloc_tile : !pto.tile_buf<loc=vec, dtype=f32, rows=16, cols=64, v_row=16, v_col=64,
                                        blayout=row_major, slayout=none_box, fractal=512, pad=0>
    %dst = pto.alloc_tile : !pto.tile_buf<loc=vec, dtype=f32, rows=16, cols=64, v_row=16, v_col=64,
                                          blayout=row_major, slayout=none_box, fractal=512, pad=0>
    %scalar = arith.constant 2.0 : f32
    pto.tdivs ins(%scalar, %a : f32,
                               !pto.tile_buf<loc=vec, dtype=f32, rows=16, cols=64, v_row=16, v_col=64,
                               blayout=row_major, slayout=none_box, fractal=512, pad=0>)
              outs(%dst : !pto.tile_buf<loc=vec, dtype=f32, rows=16, cols=64, v_row=16, v_col=64,
                                        blayout=row_major, slayout=none_box, fractal=512, pad=0>)
    return
  }
}
```

Run command (mainline-compatible):

```bash
ptoas --pto-arch=a5 test/dsl/issue_117_repro.pto > build/issue117_mainline.out 2> build/issue117_mainline.log
```

### Expected behavior

- `TDIVS_SRC_SCALAR` keeps `src / scalar`
- `TDIVS_SCALAR_SRC` keeps `scalar / src`

### Actual behavior

In `build/issue117_mainline.log`, both functions are normalized to the same textual op shape:

```text
func.func @TDIVS_SRC_SCALAR() { ... pto.tdivs ins(%0, %cst : ..., f32) ... }
func.func @TDIVS_SCALAR_SRC() { ... pto.tdivs ins(%0, %cst : ..., f32) ... }
```

This indicates `ins(%scalar, %src)` direction is not preserved.

### Suspected root cause

`TDivSOp::parse` accepts both input orders but stores operands in canonical `(src, scalar, dst)` order by swapping when scalar appears first. Downstream passes therefore cannot distinguish the two semantic directions.

### Environment

- Repo: `hw-native-sys/PTOAS` (official)
- Arch: `a5`
- Command: `ptoas --pto-arch=a5 test/dsl/issue_117_repro.pto`

title: [Bug] pto.tcolexpanddiv rejects i16/i32 on A5 during verification
body:
### Component

Verifier / IR semantics (lib/PTO/IR)

### Description

`pto.tcolexpanddiv` currently rejects integer element types during MLIR verification. On `official/main`, the verifier only accepts `f16` and `f32`, but A5 integer cases with `i16` and `i32` are expected by downstream tests and by the existing `tdiv` verifier behavior.

I confirmed this on `official/main` by checking `TColExpandDivOp::verify()`:

- `verifyTColExpandBinaryLikeOp(..., /*allowIntegerTypes=*/false)` is used for `pto.tcolexpanddiv`
- the shared helper only allows `i16/i32` when `allowIntegerTypes=true`

As a result, minimal IR with `dtype=i32` fails before tile-op-expand / lowering.

### Reproduction (minimal)

```mlir
module {
  func.func @tcolexpanddiv_i32_issue() {
    %src0 = pto.alloc_tile
      : !pto.tile_buf<loc=vec, dtype=i32, rows=16, cols=32, v_row=16, v_col=32,
                      blayout=row_major, slayout=none_box, fractal=512, pad=0>
    %src1 = pto.alloc_tile
      : !pto.tile_buf<loc=vec, dtype=i32, rows=1, cols=32, v_row=1, v_col=32,
                      blayout=row_major, slayout=none_box, fractal=512, pad=0>
    %dst = pto.alloc_tile
      : !pto.tile_buf<loc=vec, dtype=i32, rows=16, cols=32, v_row=16, v_col=32,
                      blayout=row_major, slayout=none_box, fractal=512, pad=0>

    pto.tcolexpanddiv ins(%src0, %src1 : !pto.tile_buf<loc=vec, dtype=i32, rows=16, cols=32, v_row=16, v_col=32,
                                blayout=row_major, slayout=none_box, fractal=512, pad=0>,
                            !pto.tile_buf<loc=vec, dtype=i32, rows=1, cols=32, v_row=1, v_col=32,
                                blayout=row_major, slayout=none_box, fractal=512, pad=0>)
               outs(%dst : !pto.tile_buf<loc=vec, dtype=i32, rows=16, cols=32, v_row=16, v_col=32,
                                     blayout=row_major, slayout=none_box, fractal=512, pad=0>)
    return
  }
}
```

```bash
./build/tools/ptoas/ptoas \
  --pto-arch=a5 \
  --pto-backend=vpto \
  --enable-tile-op-expand \
  --vpto-emit-hivm-llvm \
  test/dsl/issue_140_repro.pto
```

Local repro file:
- `test/dsl/issue_140_repro.pto`

### Expected behavior

`pto.tcolexpanddiv` should accept `i16` and `i32` on A5, instead of rejecting them during verification. Integer division semantics should match the intended integer divide behavior for this op.

### Actual behavior / error logs

```text
loc("test/dsl/issue_140_repro.pto":13:5): error: 'pto.tcolexpanddiv' op expects tcolexpanddiv element type to be f16 or f32
Error: Failed to parse MLIR.
```

title: [Feature] PTOAS 支持 pto-isa 中的Layout::NZ 推断
body:
### Summary

当前 PTOAS 的 Layout::NZ 推断规则，与 pto-isa 中已经定义的标准化NZ 五维表示不一致。对于 pto-isa 侧合法的NZ 五维 tensor_view，PTOAS 当前不会将其推断为 Layout::NZ，而是推断成 Layout::ND。
1.pto-isa 当前对 2D 的五维NZ 的定义：
TileShape2D<T, rows, cols, Layout::NZ> / BaseShape2D<T, rows, cols, Layout::NZ> 对二维逻辑 tensor 的五维表示为：
     shape  = [1, cols / c0, rows / 16, 16, c0]
     stride = [rows * cols, rows * c0, 16 * c0, c0, 1]
     c0 = 32 / sizeof(dtype)
例如 fp32 且 (rows, cols) = (128, 64) 时：
      shape  = [1, 8, 8, 16, 8]
      stride = [8192, 1024, 128, 8, 1]
这套定义是 pto-isa 中二维NZ的五维表示的标准形式。
2.PTOAS 当前的 NZ 推断规则
当前 PTOAS 在右对齐到五维后，判定 Layout::NZ 的关键条件是：
      shape3 == 16
      shape3 * shape4 * elemBytes == 512
      stride5 == 1
      stride4 == shape5
当前不一致现象,使用附件可进行复现：
①用例一，pto-isa canonical 2D NZ 五维形式：
      shape  = [1, 8, 8, 16, 8]
      stride = [8192, 1024, 128, 8, 1]
PTOAS 生成的 C++ 中是 pto::Layout::ND
②用例二，当前 PTOAS NZ 推断规则的五维形式
       shape = [4, 1, 16, 8, 16]
       stride = [2048, 2048, 128, 16, 1]
PTOAS 生成的 C++ 中是 pto::Layout::NZ
说明当前PTOAS 还不能把 pto-isa 的二维 NZ 的五维形式推断成 Layout::NZ

title: [Bug] tprelu triggers vec overflow on A5
body:
### Component

PTO Dialect / Memory Planning

### Description

`pto.tprelu` can trigger `vec overflow` on `main` with a single-file minimal PTO repro.

I reproduced this on `hw-native-sys/PTOAS` `main` commit `123b664a3dfb0b5113e68714799a0fedf2efbbcc` on 2026-04-21.

### Reproduction (minimal)

Save the following as `issue_116_repro.pto`:

```mlir
module {
  func.func @TPRELU_OVERFLOW() {
    %src0 = pto.alloc_tile
      : !pto.tile_buf<loc=vec, dtype=f32, rows=256, cols=200, v_row=256, v_col=200,
                      blayout=row_major, slayout=none_box, fractal=512, pad=0>
    %src1 = pto.alloc_tile
      : !pto.tile_buf<loc=vec, dtype=f32, rows=256, cols=200, v_row=256, v_col=200,
                      blayout=row_major, slayout=none_box, fractal=512, pad=0>
    %tmp = pto.alloc_tile
      : !pto.tile_buf<loc=vec, dtype=i8, rows=256, cols=200, v_row=256, v_col=200,
                      blayout=row_major, slayout=none_box, fractal=512, pad=0>
    %dst = pto.alloc_tile
      : !pto.tile_buf<loc=vec, dtype=f32, rows=256, cols=200, v_row=256, v_col=200,
                      blayout=row_major, slayout=none_box, fractal=512, pad=0>

    pto.tprelu ins(%src0, %src1, %tmp : !pto.tile_buf<loc=vec, dtype=f32, rows=256, cols=200, v_row=256, v_col=200,
                                        blayout=row_major, slayout=none_box, fractal=512, pad=0>,
                                    !pto.tile_buf<loc=vec, dtype=f32, rows=256, cols=200, v_row=256, v_col=200,
                                        blayout=row_major, slayout=none_box, fractal=512, pad=0>,
                                    !pto.tile_buf<loc=vec, dtype=i8, rows=256, cols=200, v_row=256, v_col=200,
                                        blayout=row_major, slayout=none_box, fractal=512, pad=0>)
               outs(%dst : !pto.tile_buf<loc=vec, dtype=f32, rows=256, cols=200, v_row=256, v_col=200,
                                        blayout=row_major, slayout=none_box, fractal=512, pad=0>)
    return
  }
}
```

Run:

```bash
./build/tools/ptoas/ptoas --pto-arch=a5 issue_116_repro.pto
```

### Expected behavior

The compiler should either compile successfully, or provide behavior consistent with the intended memory-planning/reuse strategy if `tprelu` at this shape is expected to be supported.

### Actual behavior / error logs

```text
loc("issue_116_repro.pto":2:3): error: vec overflow, requires 2048000 bits while 2031616 bits avaliable!
Error: Pass execution failed.
```

### Notes

- `256x192` still passes on the same build.
- `256x200` is the first shape I found that starts to fail in this local scan.
- This is a smaller standalone repro than the original ST scenario.

### Git commit

123b664a3dfb0b5113e68714799a0fedf2efbbcc

### Host platform

Ubuntu 24.04 x86_64

### Target Ascend arch (if relevant)

A5

title: Missing MTE2→V synchronization when loop body has zero iterations
[Feature] Move plan memory / insert sync from memref world to tile_buf world
body:
Suggested label: `enhancement`

## Summary

当前 PTOAS pipeline 将 `plan memory` 和 `insert sync` 放在 `View2Memref` 之后执行：

```text
[tile_buf world]
  (op fusion plan -> gen fusion region -> ...)
-> View2Memref
-> [memref world]
  (plan memory -> insert sync -> expand tileop -> ...)
```

这个 pass 边界在早期帮助我们复用 memref-world 的实现，但现在已经开始限制 tile-level 能力演进。我们希望将 `plan memory`、`insert sync` 以及与之强相关的大部分中高层 pass 前移到 `tile_buf world`，把 `View2Memref` 明确收敛为高层 Tile IR 到低层 memref IR 的边界。

目标 pipeline 形态：

```text
[tile_buf world]
  (plan memory -> insert sync -> op fusion -> expand tileop)
-> View2Memref
-> [memref world]
  (low level optimizations -> backend lowering -> ...)
```

这不是单纯的 pass 重排，而是为了让同步、融合和 TileOp 展开都发生在语义最完整的表示层上。

## Motivation / use case

### 1. 当前 pass 边界直接阻塞更高等级的 op fusion

我们希望在 `tile_buf world` 做 op fusion，因为这个阶段保留了最完整的 tile 语义信息，包括：

- tile 的布局和 config
- valid shape
- tile-level producer / consumer 关系
- 更贴近上层语义的 alias / buffer 使用形态

但 `level 3` 的 op fusion 实际上依赖 `insert sync` 的结果，因为融合不能跨越 sync point。当前 `insert sync` 位于 `memref world`，意味着 `tile_buf world` 在做融合决策时看不到最终同步边界，只能停留在不依赖 sync 结果的 `level 2` fusion。

换句话说，现有 pipeline 的问题不是“还没实现 level 3 fusion”，而是“当前 IR 分层方式让 level 3 fusion 无法在正确的位置实现”。

### 2. 当前 pipeline 让 `expand tileop` 之前发生了一次不必要的类型世界往返

`ExpandTileOp` 的模板函数接口本身就是 `Tile` / `tile_buf`。仓库里的 pass 描述也已经明确：

- `ExpandTileOp` 生成的模板函数使用 `tile_buf` 参数
- `MemrefToTileBuf` 的存在，是为了在 `PTOViewToMemref + PlanMemory + InsertSync` 之后重新恢复 `tile_buf` 语义，再继续做 Tile-level lowering

这意味着当前 pipeline 实际上在 `expand tileop` 前经历了：

```text
tile_buf -> View2Memref -> memref -> MemrefToTileBuf -> tile_buf
```

这条链路带来几个问题：

- 需要额外维护一条 `memref -> tile_buf` 的恢复路径，只是为了回到 TileOp lib 所需的接口形态
- 中间经过一次语义降级后再恢复，增加了类型、metadata、anchor 和 verifier 一致性的维护成本
- 新增 TileOp / TileBuf 能力时，需要同时考虑 lowering 和 recovery 两侧，增加系统脆弱性

如果 `plan memory` / `insert sync` 本来就是中高层语义 pass，那么让它们停留在 `tile_buf world`，可以避免这次“先降级再恢复”的往返。

### 3. 现在的分层方式已经开始影响 PTOAS 的功能完备性和稳定性

上述两个问题并不是孤立的工程不便，而是在持续影响 PTOAS 的能力边界：

- 功能完备性：sync-aware fusion、更多 tile-level 优化和更自然的 TileOp 展开都会受到限制
- 稳定性：额外的 IR world 往返意味着更多 bridge、更多隐式约束和更多恢复失败的可能性

随着 tile-level 功能继续扩展，把中高层 pass 长期放在 `memref world` 的成本只会越来越高。

## Proposed API / behavior

建议将 `tile_buf world` 和 `memref world` 的职责边界重新定义为：

- `tile_buf world`：负责高层语义相关的 memory planning、sync insertion、fusion、tileop expansion
- `memref world`：负责低层 canonicalization、backend-oriented optimization 和最终 lowering

具体上，希望逐步达成以下结果：

1. `plan memory` 在 `tile_buf world` 上工作，直接消费 Tile-level buffer / alias 信息，而不是等到 `View2Memref` 之后再规划。
2. `insert sync` 在 `tile_buf world` 上工作，使 sync point 成为 fusion 和后续高层优化可见的边界。
3. `op fusion` 在拿到 sync 信息后执行，能够支持真正受 sync point 约束的更高等级融合。
4. `expand tileop` 直接在 `tile_buf world` 完成，避免为了调用 TileOp lib 再从 memref 恢复回 `tile_buf`。
5. `View2Memref` 作为更清晰的阶段边界，只承接已经完成高层决策的 Tile IR。

如果一次性迁移过大，也可以接受分阶段演进，但最终目标应当是让 `MemrefToTileBuf` 不再承担“为高层 pass 回补语义”的核心职责。

## Additional context

仓库里已经存在一些信号，说明当前 pass 分层正在承受额外复杂度：

- `ExpandTileOp` 的描述明确指出模板函数使用 `tile_buf` 参数，并直接以 `tile_buf` 作为调用接口
- `MemrefToTileBuf` 的描述明确指出它是在 `PTOViewToMemref + PlanMemory + InsertSync` 之后恢复 `tile_buf`，以便后续 Tile->Vector lowering 继续基于 tile_buf 语义工作
- `PTOViewToMemref` 还需要专门插入 `pto.bind_tile` 作为锚点，供后续恢复 tile_buf 类型使用

这些都说明当前 pipeline 已经不是“自然地在 memref world 完成后续流程”，而是“先降到 memref world，再想办法恢复出高层 Tile 语义继续工作”。

建议把这个 issue 作为 pipeline 分层调整的总入口，后续再拆分出更细的 implementation issue，例如：

- tile_buf-world memory planning 的表示和地址回填方式
- tile_buf-world sync analysis / sync insertion
- sync-aware level 3 fusion
- `ExpandTileOp` 前移后的 pipeline 收敛
- `MemrefToTileBuf` 的降级、收缩或移除

title: [Bug] auto-sync should track aliasing through `pto.subview`
body:
### Component

PTO Dialect / ODS (include/PTO/IR)

### Description

The auto-sync pass treats the result of `pto.subset` as an independent
buffer rather than an alias of its source tile. As a consequence, no
sync flag (`set_flag` / `wait_flag` pair) is emitted between a write
to a sub-view and a later read/write of either the parent tile or an
overlapping sub-view. Kernels that use `pto.subset` to express
sub-block parallelism (each AIV sub-block owning a row-half of a
shared tile) produce wrong data.

### Reproduction (minimal)

```mlir
module {
  func.func @cube_kernel(%arg0: !pto.ptr<f32>, %arg1: !pto.ptr<f16>, %arg2: !pto.ptr<f16>, %arg3: !pto.ptr<f16>) attributes {pto.kernel_kind = #pto.kernel_kind<cube>} {

    %13 = arith.cmpi slt, %3, %5 : index

    %15 = arith.cmpi slt, %3, %5 : index
    %16 = arith.addi %4, %c1 : index

    %27 = pto.alloc_tile : !pto.tile_buf<acc, 32x256xf32, blayout=col_major, slayout=row_major, fractal=1024>
    %28 = pto.alloc_tile : !pto.tile_buf<mat, 32x256xf16, blayout=col_major, slayout=row_major>
    %29 = pto.alloc_tile : !pto.tile_buf<left, 32x256xf16, slayout=row_major>

    %c2048 = arith.constant 2048 : index

    %34 = pto.make_tensor_view %arg2, shape = [%c32_0, %c8192], strides = [%c1, %c32_0] : !pto.tensor_view<?x?xf16>
    %35 = pto.make_tensor_view %arg3, shape = [%c8192, %c32_0], strides = [%c32_0, %c1] : !pto.tensor_view<?x?xf16>
    scf.for %arg4 = %14 to %18 step %c1 {
      %36 = arith.muli %arg4, %c32 : index
      %37 = pto.partition_view %33, offsets = [%36, %c0], sizes = [%c32, %c32_0] : !pto.tensor_view<?x?xf16> -> !pto.partition_tensor_view<32x32xf16>

      pto.tmatmul ins(%24, %26 : !pto.tile_buf<left, 32x32xf16, slayout=row_major>, !pto.tile_buf<right, 32x256xf16, slayout=col_major>) outs(%27 : !pto.tile_buf<acc, 32x256xf32, blayout=col_major, slayout=row_major, fractal=1024>)
      pto.tpush_to_aiv(%27 : !pto.tile_buf<acc, 32x256xf32, blayout=col_major, slayout=row_major, fractal=1024>) {split = 0}
      %39 = pto.partition_view %35, offsets = [%c0, %c0], sizes = [%c256, %c32_0] : !pto.tensor_view<?x?xf16> -> !pto.partition_tensor_view<256x32xf16>
      pto.tload ins(%39 : !pto.partition_tensor_view<256x32xf16>) outs(%30 : !pto.tile_buf<mat, 256x32xf16, blayout=col_major, slayout=row_major>)
      scf.for %arg5 = %c1 to %c32_1 step %c1 {
        %41 = arith.muli %arg5, %c256 : index
        %42 = pto.partition_view %34, offsets = [%c0, %41], sizes = [%c32_0, %c256] : !pto.tensor_view<?x?xf16> -> !pto.partition_tensor_view<32x256xf16>
        pto.tload ins(%42 : !pto.partition_tensor_view<32x256xf16>) outs(%25 : !pto.tile_buf<mat, 32x256xf16, slayout=col_major>)

        %44 = pto.partition_view %35, offsets = [%41, %c0], sizes = [%c256, %c32_0] : !pto.tensor_view<?x?xf16> -> !pto.partition_tensor_view<256x32xf16>
        pto.tload ins(%44 : !pto.partition_tensor_view<256x32xf16>) outs(%30 : !pto.tile_buf<mat, 256x32xf16, blayout=col_major, slayout=row_major>)

        pto.tmatmul ins(%24, %26 : !pto.tile_buf<left, 32x32xf16, slayout=row_major>, !pto.tile_buf<right, 32x256xf16, slayout=col_major>) outs(%27 : !pto.tile_buf<acc, 32x256xf32, blayout=col_major, slayout=row_major, fractal=1024>)
        pto.tpush_to_aiv(%27 : !pto.tile_buf<acc, 32x256xf32, blayout=col_major, slayout=row_major, fractal=1024>) {split = 0}
      }
      %40 = pto.tpop_from_aiv {split = 0} -> !pto.tile_buf<mat, 32x256xf16, blayout=col_major, slayout=row_major>
      pto.tmov ins(%40 : !pto.tile_buf<mat, 32x256xf16, blayout=col_major, slayout=row_major>) outs(%29 : !pto.tile_buf<left, 32x256xf16, slayout=row_major>)
      pto.tfree_from_aiv{split = 0}
      pto.tmov ins(%30 : !pto.tile_buf<mat, 256x32xf16, blayout=col_major, slayout=row_major>) outs(%31 : !pto.tile_buf<right, 256x32xf16, slayout=col_major>)
      pto.tmatmul ins(%29, %31 : !pto.tile_buf<left, 32x256xf16, slayout=row_major>, !pto.tile_buf<right, 256x32xf16, slayout=col_major>) outs(%32 : !pto.tile_buf<acc, 32x32xf32, blayout=col_major, slayout=row_major, fractal=1024>)

    %23 = pto.get_subblock_idx
```

```python
sb_idx     = pto.get_subblock_idx()
row_off_sb = sb_idx * S0_HALF                       # 0 or 16

# Shared full-size tile, allocated once per func
p_fp16 = pto.alloc_tile(p_fp16_ty)                  # [S0=32, S1_TILE]

# Each sub-block grabs its own non-overlapping row-half
p_fp16_half = pto.subset(
    p_fp16,
    offsets=[row_off_sb, 0],
    sizes=[S0_HALF, S1_TILE],

# ... softmax compute writing into `p_fp16_half` ...

pto.tpush_to_aic(p_fp16, 0)                         # READ of parent
```

The RAW dependency from `tile.cvt(... p_fp16_half)` to
`pto.tpush_to_aic(p_fp16, 0)` is invisible to the auto-sync pass
because `p_fp16_half` and `p_fp16` are distinct SSA values. No flag is
emitted; the push reads stale data.

Manual `pto.pipe_barrier("V")` calls inserted at every cross-sub-block
seam reduce but do not eliminate the mismatch (because they only order
within a sub-block, not across).

## Diagnostic

To isolate the alias-tracking issue from the orthogonal "pipe ops
under sub-block parallelism" question (separate issue), I ran the
following control:

- Force both sub-blocks to compute the **upper** 16-row half
  (`row_off_sb = 0` for both).
- Only sub-block 0 commits the GM store.
- Lower 16 rows of every output block are intentionally untouched
  (≈ 50% of elements baseline-wrong).

Result: **47.8% mismatch** — i.e. less than the 50% baseline, meaning
the upper 16 rows are computed correctly. So:

- The half-view algorithm and the `pto.subset` op itself are correct.
- When both sub-blocks are also active and writing to non-overlapping
  halves of the same parent (the realistic case), mismatch jumps to
  ~64% — the cross-sub-block writes are not getting the WAR/RAW
  protection auto-sync would normally insert for the parent.

### Expected behavior

Two ops `A`, `B` accessing memory through any of:
- the parent tile `t`,
- `subset(t, ...)` or any chain of subsets rooted at `t`,

should be treated by the auto-sync dependency tracker as touching the
same memory. Standard 'set_flag / wait_flag' analysis on the parent tile. If the
subsets can be proven non-overlapping at compile time (constant
offsets + sizes), the pass may skip emitting a flag for that pair as
an optimisation.

[Bug] Non-deterministic UB allocator: identical MLIR input produces different `.cpp` outputs across runs, some of which compute incorrect results
body:
### Component

PTO Dialect / ODS (include/PTO/IR)

### Description

Running `ptoas` repeatedly on a **byte-identical** input `.pto` file produces **different `.cpp` outputs** on each invocation. The differences are not cosmetic: the UB tile base addresses (`pto.pointer_cast(%cN_i64)`) get reshuffled, and some of the resulting layouts compute **numerically wrong results** at runtime — i.e. on those layouts two logically-distinct tiles end up sharing overlapping lifetimes/storage and stomp on each other.

Concretely, on our Sinkhorn kernel:

- `md5sum sinkhorn.pto` is stable (same bytes every time the Python builder runs).
- `md5sum` of `ptoas`'s output `.cpp` differs across consecutive invocations.
- The `.so` built from the "lucky" layout passes 66/66 correctness cases at `rtol=2e-3, atol=1e-3`.
- The `.so` built from an "unlucky" layout fails 12/66 cases at the same tolerance, and **still fails 17/66 cases at the very loose `rtol=5e-2, atol=1e-2`** (so this is real wrong-arithmetic, not a precision regression).

The failures are concentrated on specific dynamic shapes (`N=4, K=32, L=64` and `N=4, K=64, L=32` for our kernel), this is consistent with an allocator-aliasing bug whose manifestation depends on which loop iteration first happens to write to the colliding tile.

This makes builds non-reproducible and silently miscompiled.

### Reproduction (minimal)

The `.pto` is generated by the PTODSL Sinkhorn builder in https://github.com/huawei-csl/pto-dsl/pull/117:

- Builder: `examples/aot/sinkhorn_dynamic_multicore/sinkhorn_builder.py`
- Generated IR (attached below): `sinkhorn.pto`

```bash
cd /mounted_home/pto-dsl/examples/aot/sinkhorn_dynamic_multicore

# 1. Confirm the input .pto is deterministic.
python3 sinkhorn_builder.py > /tmp/a.pto
python3 sinkhorn_builder.py > /tmp/b.pto
md5sum /tmp/a.pto /tmp/b.pto
#   5117399319df1c521c3fe0ee9f750e99  /tmp/a.pto
#   5117399319df1c521c3fe0ee9f750e99  /tmp/b.pto       <-- IDENTICAL

# 2. Run ptoas three times on the *same* input.
for i in 1 2 3; do
    ptoas --enable-insert-sync /tmp/a.pto -o /tmp/r$i.cpp
    md5sum /tmp/r$i.cpp
done
# Observed:
#   f4c0d4a6d4e654a9f0fe8b57f8735ce0  /tmp/r1.cpp
#   330760db3d1d225daadf92967cfc0b6e  /tmp/r2.cpp
#   dfe9db622c2d46caf0563c572cd6a233  /tmp/r3.cpp     <-- ALL DIFFERENT
```

Diffing the outputs shows the divergence is in the UB pointer-cast constants emitted at the top of the kernel, e.g.:

```bash
-  const int64_t v28 = 15392;
-  const int64_t v29 = 16416;
-  const int64_t v30 = 25632;
+  const int64_t v28 = 1024;
+  const int64_t v29 = 29888;
+  const int64_t v30 = 3104;
   ...
```

To observe the **functional** consequence (one layout correct, another broken), build twice and run the correctness tests:

```bash
bash compile.sh                                         # bad layout (example)
python ./run_sinkhorn.py --lib ./sinkhorn_lib.so --rtol 2e-3 --atol 1e-3
#   totals: {'match': 54, 'mismatch': 12, 'skip': 0}
```
```bash
bash compile.sh                                         # try again — sometimes good, sometimes bad
python ./run_sinkhorn.py --lib ./sinkhorn_lib.so --rtol 2e-3 --atol 1e-3
#   totals: {'match': 66, 'mismatch':  0, 'skip': 0}
```

title: [Bug] ptoas silently produces a hanging kernel when a tile's valid_row/valid_col is negative at runtime
body:
### Component

Verifier / IR semantics (lib/PTO/IR)

### Description

When an input `.pto` program has a tile whose dynamic `valid_row` / `valid_col` can evaluate to a **negative** value at runtime (for example, `minsi(A - k, C)` where `k > A`), `ptoas` happily generates a kernel that issues `TLOAD`/`TMOV`/`TMATMUL` with that negative valid dim. On the hardware the malformed DMA lands the pipe event scoreboard in an unrecoverable state and the kernel hangs forever — no error, no fault, no log.

The invariant `valid_row >= 0` and `valid_col >= 0` is part of the implicit contract of `pto.alloc_tile` / `pto.tload` etc., but it is nowhere enforced — neither at IR verification time, nor by a runtime guard in the generated kernel. A user who accidentally emits an overshooting driver loop (e.g. `for n in range(0, 8192 + 383, 384)` which produces `n = 8448 > 8192`) has no visible signal that anything is wrong; the only symptom is "kernel 16 never returns."

Related: #322 (verifier should reject shape mismatches on TStore), #533 (missing sync when loop zero-iterates). These all fall under the broader theme of "ptoas accepts malformed tile sizes and emits code that breaks at runtime."

### Reproduction (minimal)

Submit to `ptoas` any kernel where the allocated tile's valid dim can be negative — the pattern in real code looks like this (trimmed from a qwen3 decode kernel):

```mlir
%c8192_index  = arith.constant 8192 : index
%c384_index   = arith.constant 384  : index

// arg3 is the external loop's `n` — caller passes n = 8448 on the last iter
func.func @k(..., %arg3: index) {
  %diff  = arith.subi %c8192_index, %arg3 : index         // 8192 - 8448 = -256
  %vcol  = arith.minsi %diff, %c384_index : index         // min(-256, 384) = -256
  %tile  = pto.alloc_tile ... valid_col = %vcol
          : !pto.tile_buf<loc=mat, dtype=bf16, rows=64, cols=384, v_row=64, v_col=?, ...>
  %part  = pto.partition_view ...
  pto.tload ins(%part) outs(%tile)
  // ...tmov, tmatmul on the same tile
}
```

Compile:

```bash
ptoas input.pto -o out.cpp
```

A full reproducible case is the `Qwen3Decode` kernel 16 generated at pypto commit `103aaa94` — dump in `build_output/Qwen3Decode_20260422_122654/ptoas/qwen3_decode_incore_16.pto`, emitted kernel in the same directory's `.cpp`. Caller at `orchestration/qwen3_decode.cpp:375` passes `n = 8448` on the 23rd iteration.

### Expected behavior

Either:

1. **Compile-time** — `ptoas` does a value-range check on `valid_row`/`valid_col` operands and errors out if it can statically prove the value can be negative (e.g. `minsi(sub(const_A, x), const_C)` with no lower bound on `x`). At minimum, warn.
2. **Runtime** — generated kernel emits a guard such as
   ```cpp
   if ((int32_t)valid_col < 0 || (int32_t)valid_row < 0) {
       // either: early return (treat as no-op)
       // or:     trap / write error code + return
   }
   ```
   placed before any `TLOAD`/`TMOV`/`TMATMUL` that uses the tile. Silent hang is the worst possible failure mode.

Option 2 is strictly more actionable for users since it surfaces the bug at the first bad iteration rather than requiring the user to diff against a known-good version. Option 1 is a "nice to have" that catches a subset of cases earlier.

### Actual behavior / error logs

```text
ptoas exits 0, emits a kernel that contains e.g.:

  int32_t v31 = (int32_t)((uint32_t)v12 - (uint32_t)v4);   // 8192 - 8448 wraps: v31 = -256
  int32_t v32 = v31 < v11 ? v31 : v11;                     // v32 = -256
  Tile<..., -1, -1, ...> v33 = Tile<..., -1, -1, ...>(v23, v32);
  ...
  TLOAD(v34, v39);   // negative valid_col
  TMOV (v68, v34);
  TMATMUL_ACC(...); // hangs here / on the matching set_flag / wait_flag

Host-side: runtime sits waiting on kernel completion signal; no error reported.
```
