title: [Bug] bisheng (CANN 9.0.0-beta.1) 无法选择 intrinsic `%llvm.hivm.MOV.UB.TO.OUT.ALIGN.V2.DV`
body:
### Component

PTO Dialect / ODS (include/PTO/IR)

### Description


## 问题描述

在编译包含 `pto.tinsert` (Acc→Vec ND 路径) 的 TileLang ST 用例时，bisheng 设备编译器在 instruction selection 阶段崩溃，报告无法选择 ptoas 生成的硬件 intrinsic。

### 复现命令

```bash
source tmp/cj_mk_env.sh && ptoas_build
python test/tilelang_st/script/run_st.py -r sim -v a5 -t tinsert
```

### 错误日志

```
fatal error: error in backend: Cannot select: intrinsic %llvm.hivm.MOV.UB.TO.OUT.ALIGN.V2.DV

PLEASE submit a bug report to https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/issues/
and include the crash backtrace, preprocessed source, and associated run script.

Stack dump:
0. Program arguments: /usr/local/CANN/cann-9.0.0-beta.1/bin/bisheng 
   --target=hiipu64-hisilicon-cce -march=dav-c310-cube 
   --cce-aicore-arch=dav-c310-cube --cce-aicore-only -O2 -dc -mllvm 
   -cce-dyn-kernel-stack-size=true -c -x ir - -o <output>.o

1. Code generation
2. Running pass 'Function Pass Manager' on module '<stdin>'
3. Running pass 'HiIPU Non VF DAG->DAG Pattern Instruction Selection' 
   on function '@TINSERT_acc2vec_nd_f16_16x16_mix_aic'

Stack dump without symbol names:
/usr/local/CANN/cann-9.0.0-beta.1/bin/bisheng(_ZN4llvm16SelectionDAGISel15CannotYetSelect...)
```

---

## 根因分析

PTOAS 编译器与 CANN 设备编译器之间存在 **intrinsic 版本不兼容**：

| 组件 | 版本 | 状态 |
|------|------|------|
| ptoas (LLVM) | 19.1.7 (v0.46) | 生成 V2 intrinsic |
| bisheng (CANN) | clang 15.0.5 (cann-9.0.0-beta.1) | **不支持 V2 intrinsic** |

**问题本质**：
- ptoas 将 `pto.mte_l0c_ub` (Acc→UB 数据搬运) 下降为 LLVM IR 时，生成了硬件 intrinsic `@llvm.hivm.MOV.UB.TO.OUT.ALIGN.V2.DV`
- bisheng 后端（基于 LLVM 15.0.5）在 instruction selection 阶段无法识别该 intrinsic
- intrinsic 名称中的 `V2` 后缀表明这是较新版本的变体

---

## 触发条件

**触发路径**：必须使用 Acc→UB (L0C→UB) 数据搬运操作

**会触发的 pto op**：
- `pto.mte_l0c_ub` - 将 Acc 缓冲区数据搬到 UB 缓冲区
- 典型场景：`pto.tinsert` 中 Acc→Vec ND/DN/NZ 路径

**不会触发的操作**：
- `pto.mte_l0c_gm` - Acc 直接写回 GM（跳过 UB）
- `pto.mte_l1_ub` - L1→UB 搬运（使用不同 intrinsic）
- `pto.mte_ub_gm` - UB→GM 搬运
- `pto.textract` 的所有路径（验证回路走 `mte_l0c_gm` 或纯向量通路）

---

## 环境信息

**软件环境**：
- CANN 版本：cann-9.0.0-beta.1
- bisheng 版本：clang-5c68a1cb1231 (clang 15.0.5)
- ptoas 版本：0.46 (LLVM 19.1.7)
- OS：Linux Ubuntu (从栈帧可见 libc.so.6)

**硬件目标**：
- 架构：Hisilicon CCE (dav-c310-cube)
- 编译选项：`--cce-aicore-arch=dav-c310-cube`

---

## 影响范围

### 受影响的算子
- ✅ **tinsert**：Acc→Vec ND 路径 (`template_tinsert_acc_to_vec_nd`)
- ✅ 任何使用 `pto.mte_l0c_ub` 的自定义 TileOp

### 不受影响的算子

| 算子 | 路径 | 原因 |
|------|------|------|
| textract | Mat→Left/Right | 使用 `mte_l0c_gm` (Acc→GM) |
| textract_fp | Acc→Mat | 使用 `mte_l0c_gm` (Acc→GM) |
| textract_v2v | Vec→Vec | 纯向量通路 (`tload`→`textract`→`tstore`) |
| tmatmul | Mat×Mat | 不使用 UB 搬运输出 |
| tload/tstore | GM↔Tile | 不涉及 Acc→UB |

**验证**：textract ST 测试套件已验证可正常编译，说明问题仅限于 Acc→UB 路径。

---

## 代码位置

**触发点**：
- `lib/TileOps/tinsert_template.py:418-422` - `template_tinsert_acc_to_vec_nd` 调用 `pto.mte_l0c_ub`
- `test/tilelang_st/npu/a5/src/st/testcase/tinsert/tinsert.pto` - Case 3 & Case 6 (Acc→Vec ND kernel)

**PTO IR 示例** (会触发)：
```mlir
pto.tinsert ins(%acc_tile, %c0_idx, %c0_idx : 
                  !pto.tile_buf<acc, 16x16xf32, blayout=col_major, slayout=row_major, fractal=1024>, 
                  index, index)
            outs(%dst_vec_tile : !pto.tile_buf<vec, 16x16xf16, blayout=row_major, slayout=none_box, fractal=512>)
```

---

## 建议的修复方向

### 方案 1：升级 CANN 工具链（推荐）
升级 bisheng 至支持 `MOV.UB.TO.OUT.ALIGN.V2.DV` intrinsic 的版本。

**验证方法**：检查新版 bisheng 的 release notes 或 changelog，确认是否包含该 intrinsic 支持。

### 方案 2：PTOAS 降级 intrinsic 版本
修改 ptoas 的 lowering 逻辑，生成 V1 版本的 intrinsic（如 `MOV.UB.TO.OUT.ALIGN.DV`，无 V2 后缀）。

**风险**：V1 intrinsic 可能不支持某些特性（如对齐优化），需要验证功能完整性。

### 方案 3：规避受影响路径（临时）
从 `tinsert.pto` 中注释掉使用 `mte_l0c_ub` 的 kernel，仅测试其他路径：

```bash
# 临时禁用 Case 3 和 Case 6 (Acc→Vec ND)
# 保留 Acc→Mat 和 Vec→Vec 路径验证
```

---

## 相关测试

**可通过的测试**（不涉及 Acc→UB）：
```bash
python test/tilelang_st/script/run_st.py -r sim -v a5 -t textract
python test/tilelang_st/script/run_st.py -r sim -v a5 -t textract_fp
python test/tilelang_st/script/run_st.py -r sim -v a5 -t textract_v2v
```

**失败的测试**（涉及 Acc→UB）：
```bash
python test/tilelang_st/script/run_st.py -r sim -v a5 -t tinsert
```


### Reproduction (minimal)

```markdown
见PR：https://github.com/hw-native-sys/PTOAS/pull/765
```

### Expected behavior

without error

title: [CI] Reuse build-and-test artifacts in vpto-sim-validation and remove duplicated CI work
body:
### Summary

### Summary

The current PR CI gate does duplicated work between `build-and-test` and `vpto-sim-validation`, which makes the overall gate significantly slower than necessary.

Today these two workflows both rebuild the same PTOAS toolchain stack and also duplicate part of the validation surface:

- both prepare/restore/build LLVM
- both build/install PTOAS
- both run overlapping frontend/runtime smoke coverage around PTODSL / TileLang / end-to-end compilation flows
- `tilelang-dsl` unit coverage is also duplicated

This issue proposes:
1. reusing `build-and-test` build artifacts in `vpto-sim-validation`
2. removing low-value duplicated checks
3. keeping only the simulator-specific incremental coverage in `vpto-sim-validation`

### Motivation / use case

### Reproduction input

PR CI workflows:

- `.github/workflows/ci.yml`
- `.github/workflows/ci_sim.yml`

Relevant duplicated build sections:

`build-and-test` in `ci.yml`
- resolves/restores/builds LLVM
- builds PTOAS
- runs PTODSL tests, lit, sample tests

`vpto-sim-validation` in `ci_sim.yml`
- resolves/restores/builds LLVM again
- builds PTOAS again
- runs PyPTO smoke, VPTO SIM validation, TileLang ST, PTODSL DSL ST, tilelang-dsl unittest

Some concrete overlap points:

1. LLVM + PTOAS are built twice
- `ci.yml` `build-and-test`
- `ci_sim.yml` `vpto-sim-validation`

2. `tilelang-dsl` unit coverage is duplicated
- `ctest -L PTODSL` in `build-and-test`
- standalone `tilelang-dsl` unittest in `vpto-sim-validation`

3. PTODSL / TileLang / end-to-end smoke coverage is partially overlapping
- sample / frontend / compile-path validation in `build-and-test`
- simulator-side end-to-end smoke in `vpto-sim-validation`

### Expected performance

The PR gate should avoid rebuilding the same LLVM/PTOAS stack twice when the second workflow can consume artifacts from the first one.

Expected improvements:

- `vpto-sim-validation` should reuse PTOAS artifacts from `build-and-test`
- duplicated `tilelang-dsl` unit coverage should be removed from one side
- `vpto-sim-validation` should retain only simulator-specific incremental validation
- total PR CI wall time should drop noticeably, especially for PRs that trigger both workflows

### Actual performance

At the moment:

- `build-and-test` builds LLVM + PTOAS once
- `vpto-sim-validation` builds LLVM + PTOAS again
- some validation layers are repeated with limited incremental value
- PRs that touch VPTO / PTODSL / TileLang related paths pay for two heavyweight pipelines

### Proposed solution

#### 1. Reuse `build-and-test` artifacts in `vpto-sim-validation`

Have `build-and-test` upload a CI artifact containing at least:

- PTOAS install tree or executable payload
- any runtime libraries needed by the self-hosted simulator jobs
- optionally a minimal manifest with commit / build metadata

Candidate artifact content:

- `install-assert/`
- or `build-assert/tools/ptoas/ptoas` plus required shared libs / Python package files

Then make `vpto-sim-validation` download and use that artifact directly instead of rebuilding PTOAS.

This removes the second PTOAS build from `ci_sim.yml`.

#### 2. Keep LLVM reuse practical, but optimize for PTOAS artifact reuse first

It is acceptable if `vpto-sim-validation` still relies on self-hosted LLVM cache or local runner tool cache, but it should not rebuild PTOAS when the exact same commit was already built in `build-and-test`.

Artifact reuse should be the first optimization target because it is the cleanest cross-workflow deduplication point.

#### 3. Remove duplicated low-value checks

Suggested cleanup:

- keep `tilelang-dsl` import/unittest coverage in `build-and-test` only
- remove standalone duplicate `tilelang-dsl` unittest from `vpto-sim-validation`

This preserves basic Python-side coverage while avoiding duplicate PR cost.

#### 4. Narrow `vpto-sim-validation` to simulator-specific incremental coverage

After artifact reuse, `vpto-sim-validation` should focus on checks that `build-and-test` cannot provide well, for example:

- VPTO host simulator validation
- PyPTO simulator smoke
- PTODSL DSL ST through simulator / msprof path
- TileLang ST only if it provides simulator-specific value beyond the main CI

In other words, `vpto-sim-validation` should be the “simulator extension layer”, not a second full build-and-test pipeline.

#### 5. Optional follow-up: split `ci_sim` by sub-area

A later follow-up can refine path filters so that touching one area does not always trigger all of:
- PyPTO smoke
- VPTO SIM validation
- TileLang ST
- PTODSL DSL ST

This is useful, but artifact reuse and duplicate removal should come first.

### Non-goals

This issue does **not** propose reusing `build-and-test` artifacts in `build_wheel`.

`build_wheel` has a different packaging/distribution purpose and should remain independently validated in its own environment.

### Risks / things to validate

- artifact layout must be stable enough for self-hosted simulator jobs
- required shared libraries / Python paths must be included or reconstructed reliably
- self-hosted runner environment may still need local simulator dependencies
- if ABI / environment assumptions differ between GitHub-hosted and self-hosted runners, artifact packaging must make those differences explicit

### Suggested implementation order

1. Upload PTOAS artifact from `build-and-test`
2. Make `vpto-sim-validation` consume that artifact instead of rebuilding PTOAS
3. Remove duplicated `tilelang-dsl` unittest from `ci_sim`
4. Re-evaluate whether TileLang ST / PTODSL DSL ST still have unnecessary overlap
5. Optionally split `ci_sim` path filters into smaller subdomains

### Git commit

Current repo HEAD when filing this issue:
`<fill with git rev-parse HEAD>`

### Proposed API / behavior

_No response_

### Alternatives considered

_No response_

### Additional context

_No response_

title: [ptoas 0.45] EVENT_ID allocator reuses one global event for overlapping fences -> AIV deadlock (AICPU 507018)
body:
## Summary

ptoas (v0.45) deterministically deadlocks an AIV kernel at runtime (**AICPU 507018**) because its **hardware sync-event allocator assigns the same `EVENT_ID` to two fences that share the same `set_pipe` and have overlapping (nested) live ranges**. Two mathematically-equivalent input `.pto` programs (differing only by whether a vector `transpose` is present) assemble into AIV kernels that differ only in EVENT_ID assignment; one passes 5/5, the other deadlocks 5/5 on a2a3.

From pypto issue hw-native-sys/pypto#1789 (DeepSeek-V4 `hc_pre`). The input `.pto` contains **zero** `set_flag`/`wait_flag`/`EVENT_ID` — pypto allocates no hardware events; ptoas does all event allocation, so this is purely an allocator bug.

## Flag-identity model (from the PASS-vs-FAIL evidence)

A hardware sync flag is identified by **`(set_pipe, event_id)`** — NOT by the `(set_pipe, wait_pipe, event_id)` triple, and the `wait_pipe` is not part of the key. Two fences with the **same `set_pipe` and same `event_id`** target the **same** flag and must not have overlapping live ranges.

## The bug — failing AIV kernel `hc_pre_1spmd_aiv.cpp`

`EVENT_ID2` is assigned to a long `MTE3->V` fence **and** to an `MTE3->MTE2` fence nested inside it — both have `set_pipe = PIPE_MTE3`, so both map to the **same flag `(MTE3, EVENT_ID2)`**:

```cpp
L271   set_flag (PIPE_MTE3, PIPE_V,    EVENT_ID2);   // MTE3->V  fence opens  ┐ flag (MTE3,e2)
L524     set_flag (PIPE_MTE3, PIPE_MTE2, EVENT_ID2); //   MTE3->MTE2 opens  ┐ │ SAME flag (MTE3,e2)
L692     wait_flag(PIPE_MTE3, PIPE_MTE2, EVENT_ID2); //   MTE3->MTE2 closes ┘ │  -> nested, collides
L1242  wait_flag(PIPE_MTE3, PIPE_V,    EVENT_ID2);   // MTE3->V  closes       ┘ HANGS -> 507018
```

Live ranges on flag `(MTE3, EVENT_ID2)`: `MTE3->V = [271,1242]` strictly **contains** `MTE3->MTE2 = [524,692]`. The producer MTE3 cannot serve both consumers on one flag with this interleaving → lost wakeup → cross-pipe deadlock.

(Note: other `EVENT_ID2` ops in this kernel — e.g. `set_flag(PIPE_V, PIPE_MTE2, EVENT_ID2)`, `set_flag(PIPE_MTE2, PIPE_V, EVENT_ID2)` — are **not** part of the bug; their `set_pipe` is V / MTE2, so they are different flags `(V,e2)` / `(MTE2,e2)`.)

## Why the transpose variant passes

Same long `MTE3->V` fence, but ptoas placed it on `EVENT_ID3`, and **no other `set_pipe=MTE3` fence reuses `EVENT_ID3` within its `[271,1250]` span** (the intervening `EVENT_ID3` fences there are all V-/MTE2-sourced → different flags). The `(MTE3, *)` invariant is satisfied, so no deadlock.

## Fix — what the failing kernel should become

This **is** fixable by a local relabel: move the nested `MTE3->MTE2` fence off `EVENT_ID2` to any event whose `(MTE3, *)` flag is free over `[524,692]`. `set_pipe=MTE3` only ever uses `EVENT_ID0..3` in this kernel, and `(MTE3, EVENT_ID3)` is free over `[524,692]` (first used at L1272); `(MTE3, EVENT_ID4..7)` are entirely unused by MTE3. So:

```cpp
// before (DEADLOCK)                    // after (correct)
L524  set_flag (PIPE_MTE3, PIPE_MTE2, EVENT_ID2);   ->   set_flag (PIPE_MTE3, PIPE_MTE2, EVENT_ID4);
L692  wait_flag(PIPE_MTE3, PIPE_MTE2, EVENT_ID2);   ->   wait_flag(PIPE_MTE3, PIPE_MTE2, EVENT_ID4);
```

After this, flag `(MTE3, EVENT_ID2)` carries only the `MTE3->V` fence and flag `(MTE3, EVENT_ID4)` carries the `MTE3->MTE2` fence — no same-`set_pipe` overlap.

## Expected allocator invariant

No two fences that share a `set_pipe` and have overlapping (incl. nested) live ranges may be assigned the same `event_id`. The allocator's interference graph must add an edge between any two `set_pipe`-equal fences whose `[set_flag, wait_flag]` spans overlap.

## Reproduce

```bash
# pypto worktree @ upstream/main 6c9481b2 (built); ptoas 0.45 on PATH; pto-isa @ 8bd3ac8
export PTOAS_ROOT=.../ptoas-bin PTO_ISA_ROOT=.../pto-isa
export PYTHONPATH=.../pypto/python:$PYTHONPATH
cd pypto-lib && python models/deepseek/v4/hc_pre.py --compile-only -p a2a3 --mode decode
# transpose variant -> PASS ; direct-column-slice variant -> DEADLOCK
# diff build_output/<run>/kernels/aiv/hc_pre_1spmd_aiv.cpp
```

Full generated `hc_pre_1spmd_aiv.cpp` (PASS + DEADLOCK) and the input `.pto` (0 events) available on request.

title: [Bug] trowexpand op do not support col major tile
body:
### Component

PTO Dialect / ODS (include/PTO/IR)

### Description

`trowexpand` 系列 op（`pto.trowexpandmul`、`pto.trowexpandsub`、`pto.trowexpanddiv`）不支持 `src1` 为 col major 布局的场景。当 `src1` 的 shape 为 `[M, 1]`（per-row scalar column）且布局为 `col_major` 时，模板中对 `src1[row, :]` 的 `vlds` 调用会访问非 512B 对齐的 UB 地址，在 A5 设备上触发 error 340。

此前模板的布局约束要求所有操作数均为 `row_major`，但 Qwen3 row-expand 类 kernel 中常见的 scalar 输入布局是 `col_major, cols=1`，导致模板匹配失败或运行时访存异常。

此外，`tilelang-dsl` 的 lowering 层在生成 `vldas`/`vldus` 指令时，原有的 tile → memref → subview → castptr 路径存在结构性问题：`vldas` 只接受 `!pto.ptr` 类型，而 memref 中间表示引入了不必要的 subview 和 cast 操作，对 col major `[M, 1]` tile 的地址计算也不正确。

### Reproduction (minimal)

```markdown
使用 Qwen3 row-expand kernel，其中 `src1` 为 col major 且 shape 为 `[M, 1]`：


# src0: row_major [M, N]
# src1: col_major [M, 1]   ← per-row scalar
# dst:  row_major [M, N]
pto.trowexpandmul(src0, src1, dst)


在 A5 设备上运行会触发 error 340（非对齐访问异常）。
```

### Expected behavior

- `trowexpandmul`/`trowexpandsub`/`trowexpanddiv` 模板应同时支持 `src1` 为 `row_major` 和 `col_major` 两种布局。
- 对 `col_major` 路径，应使用非对齐访问微指令 `vldas` + `vldus` 流水线加载 scalar 向量，避免 512B 对齐限制。
- `row_major` 路径保持原有的 `vlds` 对齐访问方式不变。
- lowering 层应能将 tile 直接转换为 `!pto.ptr`（而非 memref），并通过 `arith.muli` + `arith.addi` + `pto.addptr` 正确计算元素偏移。

### Actual behavior / error logs

```text
- 模板布局约束 `_constraint_trowexpanddiv_row_major` 要求所有操作数为 `row_major`，`col_major` 的 `src1` 无法匹配。
- 即使绕过约束，运行时 `vlds` 在 col major `[M, 1]` tile 切片上访问非 512B 对齐地址，触发 error 340。
- lowering 层原有的 memref → subview → castptr 路径对 `vldas`/`vldus` 不适用，生成的 IR 结构不正确。
```

### Git commit

25d85087a66a1d4c369069a9b9b2b7c48824c824

None

### PTOAS build level (if relevant)

### Component

PTO Dialect / ODS (include/PTO/IR)

### Description

VPTO lowering pipeline 完成后，生成的 IR module 中仍残留部分 tile 元数据 op（`pto.set_valid_shape`、`pto.get_valid_shape`、`pto.treshape`、`pto.alloc_tile` 以及不再使用的 `UnrealizedConversionCastOp`）。这些 op 在 VPTO 阶段已经完成其语义功能（valid shape 信息已被消费并转化为 LLVM 可理解的 index 计算），但 LLVM 后端无法处理这些 PTO 自定义 dialect 的 op，导致 LLVM 导出失败。

具体表现为：

- `pto.set_valid_shape` 是 pure metadata op，始终没有 user，但其残留会影响 module 的合法性检查。
- `pto.get_valid_shape` 的部分 user 已完成 lowering 不再需要其输出，但 op 本身未被清理。
- `pto.treshape` 和 `pto.alloc_tile` 在 lowering 后可能失去全部 user，成为死代码。
- `UnrealizedConversionCastOp` 在类型转换完成后大量残留，其中部分用于连接 `get_valid_shape` 的 index 值与下游 LLVM i64 值的 cast 链未被折叠。

这些残留 op 导致 LLVM export 阶段报错，阻断 end-to-end 编译流水线。

### Reproduction (minimal)

```markdown
# 任意包含 tile 元数据 op 的 VPTO 输出 module
ptoas <input.pto> --emit-vpto --pto-backend=vpto --pto-level=level3
# LLVM 导出阶段报错：unhandled op in LLVM dialect conversion
```

### Expected behavior

- VPTO lowering 完成后、LLVM export 之前，应执行一次清理 pass，删除所有语义已完成且不再需要的 tile 元数据 op。
- `get_valid_shape` 的 index 值如果已有等价的 LLVM i64 值（来自原始 `alloc_tile` 的 valid row/col），应直接替换，消除不必要的 cast 链。
- 清理后的 module 不应包含任何 PTO tile metadata dialect 的 op 或悬空的 `UnrealizedConversionCastOp`。

### Actual behavior / error logs

```text
LLVM export 阶段遇到无法处理的 `pto.set_valid_shape`、`pto.get_valid_shape`、`pto.treshape`、`pto.alloc_tile` 等 op，转换失败。

### 影响范围

- `lib/PTO/Transforms/VPTOCANN900LLVMEmitter.cpp`
- `lib/PTO/Transforms/VPTOLLVMEmitter.cpp`
```

### Git commit

25d85087a66a1d4c369069a9b9b2b7c48824c824

None

### PTOAS build level (if relevant)

None

title: [Bug] pto.mgather fails on a2a3: row -> ptoas compilation failed; elem -> runtime 507018
body:
## Summary

Two well-formed `pto.mgather` kernels (emitted by PyPTO, both matching the
documented `pto.mgather` syntax) **both fail on a2a3**:

- **Case 1 — elem** (`{coalesce = #pto<coalesce elem>}`): ptoas + ccec compile
  fine, but the kernel **faults at runtime with AICore error 507018**.
- **Case 2 — row** (no coalesce attribute — the default form): **ptoas
  compilation fails**.

## Correction to the original report

The original report blamed a `{coalesce = #pto<coalesce row>}` attribute. **That
was our mistake and is NOT the bug.** PTOAS by design has **no
`{coalesce = #pto<coalesce row>}` syntax** — row is the *default* coalesce and is
emitted with **no attribute at all** (only `elem` carries
`{coalesce = #pto<coalesce elem>}`). Case 2 below uses the correct,
attribute-free row form and **still** fails ptoas compilation, so the failure is
unrelated to the coalesce attribute.

## Environment

- ptoas **v0.45**; target **a2a3**; flags `--enable-insert-sync --pto-level=level3 --pto-arch a3`; pto-isa latest main.

---

## Case 1 — elem mode → runtime 507018

`dst[i, j] = mem[idx[i, j]]`, mem `[256]`, idx `[8,32]`, dst `[8,32]`.

```mlir

  %c32_index = arith.constant 32 : index

  %idx_tensor__ssa_v0_view = pto.make_tensor_view %arg1, shape = [%c8_index, %c32_index], strides = [%c32_index, %c1_index] {layout = #pto.layout<nd>}: !pto.tensor_view<?x?xi32>
  %output__ssa_v0_view = pto.make_tensor_view %arg2, shape = [%c8_index, %c32_index], strides = [%c32_index, %c1_index] {layout = #pto.layout<nd>}: !pto.tensor_view<?x?xf32>
  %idx_tile__ssa_v0 = pto.alloc_tile addr = %c0_i64 valid_row = %c8_index valid_col = %c32_index : !pto.tile_buf<loc=vec, dtype=i32, rows=8, cols=32, v_row=?, v_col=?, blayout=row_major, slayout=none_box, fractal=512, pad=0>

  pto.tload ins(%idx_tensor__ssa_v0_pview : !pto.partition_tensor_view<8x32xi32>) outs(%idx_tile__ssa_v0 : !pto.tile_buf<loc=vec, dtype=i32, rows=8, cols=32, v_row=?, v_col=?, blayout=row_major, slayout=none_box, fractal=512, pad=0>)
  %dst__ssa_v0 = pto.alloc_tile addr = %c0_i64 valid_row = %c8_index valid_col = %c32_index : !pto.tile_buf<loc=vec, dtype=f32, rows=8, cols=32, v_row=?, v_col=?, blayout=row_major, slayout=none_box, fractal=512, pad=0>
  %mem_tensor__ssa_v0_pview = pto.partition_view %mem_tensor__ssa_v0_view, offsets = [%c0_index], sizes = [%c256_index] : !pto.tensor_view<?xf32> -> !pto.partition_tensor_view<256xf32>
  pto.mgather ins(%mem_tensor__ssa_v0_pview, %idx_tile__ssa_v0 : !pto.partition_tensor_view<256xf32>, !pto.tile_buf<loc=vec, dtype=i32, rows=8, cols=32, v_row=?, v_col=?, blayout=row_major, slayout=none_box, fractal=512, pad=0>) outs(%dst__ssa_v0 : !pto.tile_buf<loc=vec, dtype=f32, rows=8, cols=32, v_row=?, v_col=?, blayout=row_major, slayout=none_box, fractal=512, pad=0>) {coalesce = #pto<coalesce elem>}
  %output__ssa_v0_pview = pto.partition_view %output__ssa_v0_view, offsets = [%c0_index, %c0_index], sizes = [%c8_index, %c32_index] : !pto.tensor_view<?x?xf32> -> !pto.partition_tensor_view<8x32xf32>
  pto.tstore ins(%dst__ssa_v0 : !pto.tile_buf<loc=vec, dtype=f32, rows=8, cols=32, v_row=?, v_col=?, blayout=row_major, slayout=none_box, fractal=512, pad=0>) outs(%output__ssa_v0_pview : !pto.partition_tensor_view<8x32xf32>)
  return
  }

**Failure:** ptoas + ccec succeed (codegen_errors.txt empty), but on-device:
```
RuntimeError: run_prepared failed with code 507018
[ERROR] sync_run_streams: aclrtSynchronizeStreamWithTimeout (AICPU) failed: 507018
```
(device marked unrecoverable + force-reset).

---

## Case 2 — row mode → ptoas compilation failed

`dst[r, j] = mem[idx[r], j]`, mem `[64,32]` (f16), idx `[1,16]`, dst `[16,32]`.
Note: row is the default coalesce, so **no coalesce attribute** is emitted.

  %idx_tensor__ssa_v0_view = pto.make_tensor_view %arg1, shape = [%c1_index, %c16_index], strides = [%c16_index, %c1_index] {layout = #pto.layout<nd>}: !pto.tensor_view<?x?xi32>
  %output__ssa_v0_view = pto.make_tensor_view %arg2, shape = [%c16_index, %c32_index], strides = [%c32_index, %c1_index] {layout = #pto.layout<nd>}: !pto.tensor_view<?x?xf16>
  %idx_tile__ssa_v0 = pto.alloc_tile addr = %c0_i64 valid_row = %c1_index valid_col = %c16_index : !pto.tile_buf<loc=vec, dtype=i32, rows=1, cols=16, v_row=?, v_col=?, blayout=row_major, slayout=none_box, fractal=512, pad=0>
  %idx_tensor__ssa_v0_pview = pto.partition_view %idx_tensor__ssa_v0_view, offsets = [%c0_index, %c0_index], sizes = [%c1_index, %c16_index] : !pto.tensor_view<?x?xi32> -> !pto.partition_tensor_view<1x16xi32>
  pto.tload ins(%idx_tensor__ssa_v0_pview : !pto.partition_tensor_view<1x16xi32>) outs(%idx_tile__ssa_v0 : !pto.tile_buf<loc=vec, dtype=i32, rows=1, cols=16, v_row=?, v_col=?, blayout=row_major, slayout=none_box, fractal=512, pad=0>)
  %dst__ssa_v0 = pto.alloc_tile addr = %c64_i64 valid_row = %c16_index valid_col = %c32_index : !pto.tile_buf<loc=vec, dtype=f16, rows=16, cols=32, v_row=?, v_col=?, blayout=row_major, slayout=none_box, fractal=512, pad=0>

  pto.mgather ins(%mem_tensor__ssa_v0_pview, %idx_tile__ssa_v0 : !pto.partition_tensor_view<64x32xf16>, !pto.tile_buf<loc=vec, dtype=i32, rows=1, cols=16, v_row=?, v_col=?, blayout=row_major, slayout=none_box, fractal=512, pad=0>) outs(%dst__ssa_v0 : !pto.tile_buf<loc=vec, dtype=f16, rows=16, cols=32, v_row=?, v_col=?, blayout=row_major, slayout=none_box, fractal=512, pad=0>)
  %output__ssa_v0_pview = pto.partition_view %output__ssa_v0_view, offsets = [%c0_index, %c0_index], sizes = [%c16_index, %c32_index] : !pto.tensor_view<?x?xf16> -> !pto.partition_tensor_view<16x32xf16>
  pto.tstore ins(%dst__ssa_v0 : !pto.tile_buf<loc=vec, dtype=f16, rows=16, cols=32, v_row=?, v_col=?, blayout=row_major, slayout=none_box, fractal=512, pad=0>) outs(%output__ssa_v0_pview : !pto.partition_tensor_view<16x32xf16>)

```

**Failure:**
```
ERROR pypto.backend.pto_backend:pto_backend.py:1031 Failed to compile function 'mgather_kernel': ptoas compilation failed:
```
`report/codegen_errors.txt` contains only `ptoas compilation failed:` with no
further diagnostic — running `ptoas` directly on this `.pto` aborts (SIGABRT /
core dump, exit 134) with no message.

---

## Expected

Both forms should lower and run on a2a3 (`dst[r,j]=mem[idx[r],j]` for row,
`dst[i,j]=mem[idx[i,j]]` for elem). At minimum, ptoas should emit a clear
diagnostic instead of aborting with no message (Case 2) or producing a kernel
that 507018s on device (Case 1).

title: [Bug] a2a3 onboard MGATHER coalesce=elem faults at runtime (AICore 507018); ptoas compile OK
body:
## Summary

A `pto.mgather` with `{coalesce = #pto<coalesce elem>}` (`dst[i,j] = mem[idx[i,j]]`)
**compiles cleanly** through ptoas + ccec for **a2a3**, but **faults at runtime
on real silicon with AICore error 507018** (`aclrtSynchronizeStreamWithTimeout
(AICPU) failed: 507018`; the device is poisoned and force-reset).

> Note on routing: ptoas itself is **not** at fault here — it lowers the op fine
> and emits a clean `MGATHER<pto::Coalesce::Elem>(...)` call. The runtime fault is
> in the **pto-isa a2a3 onboard `MGatherElemImpl`** template (or the launch). Filed
> here for triage; please route to pto-isa if appropriate. (The companion
> ptoas-side crash is the separate row-mode issue.)

## Environment

- ptoas: **0.45**
- pto-isa: `e25732f0` (latest main — required; older main A5-gated the templated `MGATHER<Coalesce>` so a2a3 ccec failed with "no matching function for 'MGATHER<Coalesce::Elem>'")
- Target: a2a3 (Ascend 910B/C), on-board device run
- Flags: `--enable-insert-sync --pto-level=level3 --pto-arch a3`

## Failing `.pto` (elem mode: `dst[i,j] = mem[idx[i,j]]`, mem `[256]`, idx `[8,32]`, dst `[8,32]`)

```mlir
module attributes {pto.target_arch = "a2a3"} {
  func.func @mgather_kernel(%arg0: !pto.ptr<f32>, %arg1: !pto.ptr<i32>, %arg2: !pto.ptr<f32>) attributes {pto.kernel_kind = #pto.kernel_kind<vector>} {
  %c0_i64 = arith.constant 0 : i64
  %c256_index = arith.constant 256 : index
  %c1_index = arith.constant 1 : index
  %c8_index = arith.constant 8 : index
  %c32_index = arith.constant 32 : index
  %c0_index = arith.constant 0 : index
  %mem_tensor__ssa_v0_view = pto.make_tensor_view %arg0, shape = [%c256_index], strides = [%c1_index] {layout = #pto.layout<nd>}: !pto.tensor_view<?xf32>
  %idx_tensor__ssa_v0_view = pto.make_tensor_view %arg1, shape = [%c8_index, %c32_index], strides = [%c32_index, %c1_index] {layout = #pto.layout<nd>}: !pto.tensor_view<?x?xi32>
  %output__ssa_v0_view = pto.make_tensor_view %arg2, shape = [%c8_index, %c32_index], strides = [%c32_index, %c1_index] {layout = #pto.layout<nd>}: !pto.tensor_view<?x?xf32>
  %idx_tile__ssa_v0 = pto.alloc_tile addr = %c0_i64 valid_row = %c8_index valid_col = %c32_index : !pto.tile_buf<loc=vec, dtype=i32, rows=8, cols=32, v_row=?, v_col=?, blayout=row_major, slayout=none_box, fractal=512, pad=0>
  %idx_tensor__ssa_v0_pview = pto.partition_view %idx_tensor__ssa_v0_view, offsets = [%c0_index, %c0_index], sizes = [%c8_index, %c32_index] : !pto.tensor_view<?x?xi32> -> !pto.partition_tensor_view<8x32xi32>
  pto.tload ins(%idx_tensor__ssa_v0_pview : !pto.partition_tensor_view<8x32xi32>) outs(%idx_tile__ssa_v0 : !pto.tile_buf<loc=vec, dtype=i32, rows=8, cols=32, v_row=?, v_col=?, blayout=row_major, slayout=none_box, fractal=512, pad=0>)
  %dst__ssa_v0 = pto.alloc_tile addr = %c0_i64 valid_row = %c8_index valid_col = %c32_index : !pto.tile_buf<loc=vec, dtype=f32, rows=8, cols=32, v_row=?, v_col=?, blayout=row_major, slayout=none_box, fractal=512, pad=0>
  %mem_tensor__ssa_v0_pview = pto.partition_view %mem_tensor__ssa_v0_view, offsets = [%c0_index], sizes = [%c256_index] : !pto.tensor_view<?xf32> -> !pto.partition_tensor_view<256xf32>
  pto.mgather ins(%mem_tensor__ssa_v0_pview, %idx_tile__ssa_v0 : !pto.partition_tensor_view<256xf32>, !pto.tile_buf<loc=vec, dtype=i32, rows=8, cols=32, v_row=?, v_col=?, blayout=row_major, slayout=none_box, fractal=512, pad=0>) outs(%dst__ssa_v0 : !pto.tile_buf<loc=vec, dtype=f32, rows=8, cols=32, v_row=?, v_col=?, blayout=row_major, slayout=none_box, fractal=512, pad=0>) {coalesce = #pto<coalesce elem>}
  %output__ssa_v0_pview = pto.partition_view %output__ssa_v0_view, offsets = [%c0_index, %c0_index], sizes = [%c8_index, %c32_index] : !pto.tensor_view<?x?xf32> -> !pto.partition_tensor_view<8x32xf32>
  pto.tstore ins(%dst__ssa_v0 : !pto.tile_buf<loc=vec, dtype=f32, rows=8, cols=32, v_row=?, v_col=?, blayout=row_major, slayout=none_box, fractal=512, pad=0>) outs(%output__ssa_v0_pview : !pto.partition_tensor_view<8x32xf32>)
  return
  }
}
```

## Generated kernel (looks correct)

ccec compiles it cleanly; the emitted call and the GlobalTensor for the 1-D
`mem[256]` look correct:

```cpp
// mem[256] -> rank-5 ND GlobalTensor <1,1,1,1,256>
GlobalTensor<float, pto::Shape<1,1,1,1,256>, pto::Stride<256,256,256,256,1>, pto::Layout::ND> v25 = ...;
MGATHER<pto::Coalesce::Elem>(v18 /*dst Tile<Vec,f32,8,32>*/, v25 /*table*/, v9 /*idx Tile<Vec,i32,8,32>*/);
```

Tracing `MGATHER_IMPL` (a2a3 `MGather.hpp`): `validRow/validCol = dst.GetValidRow()/GetValidCol()` (runtime 8/32, correct loop bound), `tableSize = product of GlobalTensor dims = 256` (correct), and for the default `GatherOOB::Undefined` the remap sets `doRead=1` so all in-bounds `idx ∈ [0,256)` reads are valid. There is no obvious runaway loop or OOB — yet it still 507018s on-device.

## Repro

```bash
# build_output/mgather_elem_fp32_*/  produced by the PyPTO ST run; ptoas+ccec succeed,
# then on-device:
pytest tests/st/runtime/ops/test_mgather.py::TestMgatherElem::test_fp32 --forked -v --platform=a2a3 --save-kernels --device <N>
# -> RuntimeError: aclrtSynchronizeStreamWithTimeout (AICPU) failed: 507018
```

## Notes

- The 507018 is on a **clean card** (the row-mode cases fail at compile and never
  reach the device, so this is genuinely the elem kernel's fault, not a poison
  cascade).
- The recent pto-isa MGather commits are **CPU_SIM / sim** focused
  (`[CPU_SIM] New MGather/MScatter`, `fix(sim): Align non-templated
  MGATHER/MSCATTER default to hardware Row`), so the **a2a3 onboard** MGather
  path may be unvalidated on real silicon.

## Expected

`MGATHER<Coalesce::Elem>` should execute correctly on a2a3 hardware
(`dst[i,j] = mem[idx[i,j]]`), matching the CPU-sim reference.

title: [Pass Bug] pto-insert-sync drops PIPE_MTE3<->PIPE_V WAR sync on valid MemoryReuse relayout -> stale read
body:
## Summary `pto-insert-sync` (the `--enable-insert-sync` / `PTOInsertSync` pass, **ptoas 0.45**) drops a required **`PIPE_MTE3` ↔ `PIPE_V` WAR synchronization** when the input `.pto` packs vec/UB tiles into a tighter (but lifetime-valid) layout. A vector op in the next loop iteration then overwrites a buffer before the `MTE3` store that drains it has finished reading → stale read → deterministically wrong output (~17.5% mismatch on the dsv4 `prefill_sparse_attn` kernel, a2a3). Two `.pto` for the same kernel (`prefill_hca_attn_qk_softmax_tile`) differ **only** in vec tile addresses (a valid pypto `MemoryReuse` relayout). Running the *same* ptoas command on each: | layout | vec tile addrs (v25..v29) | `PIPE_MTE3`↔`PIPE_V` flags emitted | |---|---|---| | working (pre-relayout) | `81920 / 73728 / 65536 / 81984 / 90176` (disjoint) | **8** ✅ | | **failing (attached below)** | `69696 / 65536 / 69760 / 65600 / 77952` (packed/overlapping) | **4** ❌ | Sync correctness must be invariant to a valid address relayout; here it is not. Concretely, the store of `softmax_mi` at addr **65536** loses its trailing `set_flag(PIPE_MTE3, PIPE_V)`, and the next-iteration vector write to 65536 loses its `wait_flag(PIPE_MTE3, PIPE_V)`: ```c // failing: loop top is missing set_flag(PIPE_MTE3, PIPE_V, EVENT_ID0); TSTORE(v77, v61); // v61 @ 65536 (softmax_mi) -> GM prefill_blk_mi ; MTE3 reads 65536 // <-- set_flag(PIPE_MTE3, PIPE_V) MISSING here // next iteration's V write to 65536 has no wait_flag(PIPE_MTE3, PIPE_V) ``` Race: V pipe (iter N+1 `trowmax`) overwrites 65536 before MTE3 (iter N store) drains it → `prefill_blk_mi/li`, `prefill_exp` get cross-iteration stale data. ## Root-cause analysis (from reading ptoas source @ `f583ed6a`) With `--pto-insert-sync-debug=3` on both layouts, `MemoryDependentAnalyzer::MemAlias` reports **zero** address-range matches for local (vec/UB) memory (only `Real roots differ` / `Scope Mismatch`). The final sync counts differ (`set/wait` 13/13 working vs 11/11 failing), and the gap is already present **before** `RemoveRedundantSync` — i.e. the dependency graph itself under-computes 2 `MTE3`↔`V` hazards for the failing layout. Cause: in `lib/PTO/Transforms/InsertSync/PTOIRTranslator.cpp::UpdateAllocTileOpMemInfo`, every `pto.alloc_tile` is registered with `rootBuffer = res` (itself). In `MemoryDependentAnalyzer::MemAlias` (local-memory branch), the `isBufferAddressRangeOverlap` path is only reached when `a->rootBuffer == b->rootBuffer` or `GetRealRoot(a) == GetRealRoot(b)`. Two **distinct** `alloc_tile`s never share a root (no view chain links them), so the absolute-`baseAddresses` range-overlap check (`isBufferOverlap`: `maxStart < minEnd`) is effectively **dead code** for vec/UB. Local-memory WAR/WAW detection then relies solely on exact address-key def/use in the SyncIR — which the relayout breaks, silently missing a real hazard. Suggested fix: make local-memory anti-dependency detection do real `baseAddresses` + `allocateSize` range-overlap within the same address space, independent of `rootBuffer` identity (i.e. let the existing `isBufferOverlap` machinery run for vec/UB). ## Git commit ptoas `0.45` (binary). Source read at `f583ed6a`. ## Target Ascend arch a3 (a2a3) ## PTOAS build level level3 ## Additional context - Discovered as a numerical regression in pypto: bisected to pypto `MemoryReuse` PR #1805 ("global largest-first packing"), which changed **only** vec tile addresses. pypto emits no sync at all in `.pto`; ptoas owns all pipe-sync insertion, so the layout is valid and the missed sync is on the ptoas side. - Repro kernel: `models/deepseek/v4/prefill_sparse_attn.py` (open-source, `hw-native-sys/pypto-lib`); on-device symptom: `attn_out` fails `ratio_allclose(atol=1e-4, rtol=1/128)`, error_count ≈ 92186/524288 (~17.58%), deterministic.

title: PTOViewToMemref should canonicalize addptr uniformly for low-level pointer consumers
body:
## Problem

`pto.addptr` is currently handled in `PTOViewToMemref` in a consumer-specific way. The existing folding logic only covers a small whitelist of users such as:

- `make_tensor_view`
- scalar load/store
- a few initialization ops

When an `addptr` result is consumed directly by other low-level pointer users, especially memory-transfer style ops, the offset is not canonicalized into the memref/view world early enough. The later cleanup path then either leaves the `addptr` stranded or reports an unsupported pattern.

This makes `addptr` support fragile: whether a program works depends on which op happens to consume the pointer, not on whether the pointer arithmetic itself is semantically valid.

## Why this matters

This is a general compiler pipeline issue rather than a testcase-specific one:

- frontends can legitimately produce `ptr<gm>` plus offset and feed it into low-level ops
- new ops may hit the same failure unless they are added to another ad hoc whitelist
- fixing this per consumer is easy to miss and does not scale

## Suggested direction

Handle `pto.addptr` with a uniform canonicalization rule in `PTOViewToMemref` instead of special-casing individual consumers.

A more robust approach would be:

1. Convert `addptr(base, offset)` into an offset-bearing memref/view representation as early as possible.
2. Let downstream passes operate on that canonical representation.
3. Only lower back to raw pointer arithmetic at the final stage if the backend still requires raw pointers.

`memref.subview` or an equivalent view-like representation should be sufficient for most cases.

## Expected benefit

- `addptr` semantics become independent of the specific consumer op
- fewer consumer-specific folds in `PTOViewToMemref`
- better coverage for future low-level ops without additional pass patches
- easier reasoning about pointer offsets across the pipeline

title: MGATHER row mode races on a2a3: PTOAS inserts no MTE2->S for the scalar index read (missing SyncMacroModel)
body:
## Summary

On a2a3, `pto.mgather` in **row** mode produces wrong gathered rows or hangs the
AICore (507018), nondeterministically across runs (same case flips between hang
and wrong-values = a data race). **Elem** mode works. Root cause is a
cross-pipe synchronization that **PTOAS should insert but currently does not**.

## Root cause (PTOAS sync modeling)

MGATHER reads its **index tile on the SCALAR (S) pipe** (`idxPtr[r]`) to compute
GM addresses. But `MGatherOp::getPipe()` returns a single pipe = `PIPE_MTE2`
(`include/PTO/IR/PTOOps.td:2856`), and the sync translator
(`PTOIRTranslator::getOpPipeline`) models **all** of mgather's operand reads as
happening on that one pipe (MTE2).

The `idx` tile is produced by `pto.tload` (MTE2). So the sync solver sees
producer MTE2 -> consumer MTE2 and inserts only an **MTE2<->MTE2 `pipe_barrier`**
— it never inserts **MTE2 -> S**. The scalar idx read therefore races the idx
DMA -> stale/garbage indices -> wrong rows or out-of-bounds addresses (507018).

This is the same class of op as `TScatter`/`TGather` (which also read indices on
the scalar pipe) — and those **already have a `SyncMacroModel`**
(`lib/PTO/Transforms/InsertSync/SyncMacroModel.cpp`). `MGatherOp` has none.

`MGatherElemImpl` "works" only because the pto-isa template currently hand-codes
`PtoSetWaitFlag<PIPE_MTE2, PIPE_S>()`; `MGatherRowImpl` does not. That manual
sync is the **wrong layer** — it should be PTOAS's job.

## Proposed fix (PTOAS owns the sync)

Add a `SyncMacroModel` for `MGatherOp`, mirroring `getTScatterSyncMacroModel` /
`getTGatherSyncMacroModel`, so the solver learns the real per-pipe usage and
inserts the MTE2->S wait automatically.

`lib/PTO/Transforms/InsertSync/SyncMacroModel.cpp` (anonymous namespace):

```cpp
std::optional<SyncMacroModel> getMGatherSyncMacroModel(pto::MGatherOp op) {
  // A5 lowers via the vector path (getPipe()==PIPE_V); no scalar idx loop.
  if (getTargetArch(op.getOperation()) == PTOArch::A5)
    return std::nullopt;

  const bool isElem = op.getCoalesce() == pto::Coalesce::Elem;  // no attr => Row
  SyncMacroModel model;
  if (isElem) {
    // Elem: scalar idx read + scalar GM element loads + scalar dst writes (S).
    addPhase(model, PipelineType::PIPE_S, ValueRange{op.getDst()},
             ValueRange{op.getIdx(), op.getMem()});
  } else {
    // Row: PIPE_S reads idx to compute addresses, then MTE2 DMAs each row.
    addPhase(model, PipelineType::PIPE_S, ValueRange{}, ValueRange{op.getIdx()});
    addPhase(model, PipelineType::PIPE_MTE2, ValueRange{op.getDst()},
             ValueRange{op.getMem()});
    addHiddenEvent(model, PipelineType::PIPE_S, PipelineType::PIPE_MTE2,
                   ArrayRef<unsigned>{0});
  }
  return model;
}
```

Register it in `getSyncMacroModel`:

```cpp
  if (auto tgather = dyn_cast<pto::TGatherOp>(op))
    return getTGatherSyncMacroModel(tgather);
  if (auto mgather = dyn_cast<pto::MGatherOp>(op))   // new
    return getMGatherSyncMacroModel(mgather);
```

The load-bearing line is `addPhase(..., PIPE_S, ..., {op.getIdx()})` — it makes
the solver emit `tload(MTE2) -> mgather(S)`. The exact phase decomposition for
`dst`/`mem` and hidden events can be refined by whoever owns the MGATHER codegen.

Then **pto-isa removes its manual sync**: delete the `PtoSetWaitFlag<...>()`
prologue/epilogue from `MGatherRowImpl`, `MGatherRowNzImpl`, `MGatherElemImpl`,
`MGatherElemNzImpl` in `include/pto/npu/a2a3/MGather.hpp` (now PTOAS-owned).

## Evidence (a2a3, isolated per-case on a freshly reset device)

- row FP32 leading / reversed idx: 507018 hang
- row FP32 / FP16 random idx: wrong values (480/512 mismatched)
- row FP32 large (mem [128,64], 32 rows): wrong values (1088/2048)
- elem FP32 / FP16 / INT32 (incl. valid<physical): PASS
- the SAME row case flips between 507018 and wrong-values across runs -> race
- **device-verified**: hand-adding `PtoSetWaitFlag<PIPE_MTE2, PIPE_S>()` to
  `MGatherRowImpl` flips all 5 failing row cases to PASS (5 fail -> 0 fail) ->
  proves the only defect is the missing MTE2->S, which PTOAS should insert.

The generated `.cpp` / `.pto` for row vs elem are identical except shapes and the
`Coalesce` template arg -> codegen is correct; the gap is purely the sync.

## Environment

- Arch: a2a3
- ptoas: v0.46
- pto-isa: b2d297e1
- Flags: `--enable-insert-sync --pto-level=level3 --pto-arch a3`

Context: pypto `tile.mgather` (hw-native-sys/pypto#1807, PR #1812). Supersedes
the (now-closed) pto-isa-side issue — the fix belongs in PTOAS auto-sync.

title: [Bug] ptoas codegen generates dead TMOV self-copy and redundant pipe_barrier in AIV v_proj_vec_rs kernel
body:
### Diagnosis

**ptoas** — The generated kernel file header says "Generated by PyPTO IR Compiler (PTO backend)" / "ptoas-generated code". The dead TMOV self-copy and redundant pipe_barrier(PIPE_V) are emitted by ptoas's codegen pass.

### Description

ptoas generates dead `TMOV` self-copy instructions and redundant `pipe_barrier(PIPE_V)` in the AIV `v_proj_vec_rs` kernel.

**Reproduction:**
1. Build a model with `V_PROJ_ON_AIV=1` (e.g. Qwen3-14B decode layer)
2. Run `python decode_layer.py -p a2a3 -d 0 --fwd-layers 2`
3. Inspect the generated kernel at `build_output/_jit_decode_fwd_*/kernels/aiv/v_proj_vec_rs.cpp`

**Issue 1: Dead TMOV self-copy (320 instances)**

Inside the inner N-column loop (executed 160 times × 2 groups = 320 total), ptoas emits:

```cpp
// Line 165-169 (first group), repeated symmetrically at line 226-230
Tile<..., 16, 16> v77 = ...;
TASSIGN(v77, v78);           // v78 = 65600 (v22)
pipe_barrier(PIPE_V);
TMOV(v77, v28);              // v28@65600 → v77@65600 — SELF-COPY, v77 never read again
```

`v28` (the accumulator) is assigned to UB address 65600 (line 76, `TASSIGN(v28, v22=65600)`). `v77` is assigned to the **same address** 65600 (`v78 = v22 = 65600`). `TMOV(v77, v28)` copies 65600→65600 (a self-copy), and `v77` is never read by any subsequent instruction — the next loop iteration redeclares it.

This produces 320 dead `TMOV` instructions, each accompanied by:
- 1 redundant `Tile` declaration
- 1 redundant `TASSIGN`
- 1 redundant `pipe_barrier(PIPE_V)`

Total dead code: ~960 lines of useless instructions + 320 useless memory copies.

**Issue 2: Redundant pipe_barrier(PIPE_V) (~1001 instances)**

All `pipe_barrier(PIPE_V)` in the kernel are intra-pipe (PIPE_V → PIPE_V) dependencies. Ascend's vector pipeline executes instructions in order — same-pipe RAW hazards are tracked by hardware scoreboard automatically. No explicit synchronization is needed.

The only barriers that are actually needed are cross-pipe (MTE2→V, V→MTE3), which are already correctly handled with `set_flag`/`wait_flag`.

Example (line 143-144):
```cpp
pipe_barrier(PIPE_V);               // ← redundant
TCOLEXPANDMUL(v64, v53, v62);       // reads v62, written by TEXTRACT(v62) on line 139 — same Tile, same pipe
```

The barriers serialize the pipeline, destroying instruction-level parallelism. `pipe_barrier(PIPE_V)` flushes the entire V pipeline, whereas the same-pipe ordering guarantee needs no software intervention.

### Environment

| Component | Version |
|---|---|
| pypto-lib | `e5be60b` |
| pypto | `482c17d` (branch: main) |
| pypto runtime (submodule) | `b7d04b4` |
| pto-isa | `e25732f` |
| ptoas | 0.45 |
| CANN | not detected |

### Host Platform

Linux (aarch64)

### Additional Context

Affected file: `build_output/_jit_decode_fwd_20260626_172440/kernels/aiv/v_proj_vec_rs.cpp` (286 lines)

Also observed in earlier build: `build_output/_jit_decode_fwd_layers_20260623_202600/kernels/aiv/v_proj_vec_rs.cpp` (identical codegen).

title: Chunked pto.comm.tput (staging tile smaller than transfer) does not drain its stores before a following TNOTIFY → peer reads partial data (a2a3)
body:
## Summary

When the VEC staging tile passed to `pto::comm::TPUT` is **smaller than the transfer extent** (so TPUT internally 2-D-slides the transfer through the tile in multiple chunks), the generated kernel does **not** drain the chunked MTE3 stores before a following cross-rank `pto::comm::TNOTIFY`. The signal therefore races ahead of the last in-flight chunk stores; the peer's `TWAIT` unblocks and reads **partial data**.

Single-shot TPUT (staging tile == transfer extent) does **not** exhibit this — it is self-draining.

This is the same insert-sync / `pto.comm.tput` hazard family as #706 and #730, but specific to the **chunked (sub-tile staging)** TPUT path.

## Repro

Frontend (PyPTO) — a 2-rank ring-shuffle `pld.tensor.put` of an `[8, 64]` FP32 window, with the staging tile forced down to `[2, 64]` (or `[2, 32]`) so TPUT must auto-chunk:

- rank `r` pushes its `[8,64]` slice into peer `(r+1)%2`'s slice, then `TNOTIFY`s the peer; peer `TWAIT`s then reads its slice back.
- Golden: `out[r] == in[(r-1)%2]`.

Observed on **device (a2a3 / Ascend 910B, 2 ranks)**:
- **chunked** staging (`[2,32]` or `[2,64]` tile, full `[8,64]` transfer) → **wrong**: one direction fully correct, the other has the **top rows correct and the bottom rows zero** (a partial transfer; `max diff = 511`). Reproduced with both column-split and row-only chunking.
- **single-shot** staging (full `[8,64]` tile) → **correct**.

## Generated C++ (PTOAS output)

The chunked TPUT region (`next_levels/chip_orch/kernels/aiv/ring_step.cpp`). Note the GlobalTensor is the **full** `Shape<1,1,1,8,64>` transfer while the staging tile is `Tile<...,2,32,...,-1,-1,...>` (allocated 2x32, `ValidRow=ValidCol=-1` = DYNAMIC):

```cpp
GlobalTensor<float, Shape<1,1,1,8,64>, Stride<512,512,512,64,1>, Layout::ND> v36 = ...;  // full transfer
// v28 = Tile<TileType::Vec, float, 2, 32, RowMajor, -1, -1, NoneBox, ...>               // sub-tile staging

pipe_barrier(PIPE_ALL);                          // orders the preceding source TSTORE (ok)
wait_flag(PIPE_MTE3, PIPE_MTE2, EVENT_ID1);
pto::comm::TPUT(v36, v26, v28);                  // chunked: 4x2 internal slide, many MTE3 stores
set_flag(PIPE_MTE3, PIPE_MTE2, EVENT_ID2);
// >>> nothing drains the chunked stores here <<<
pto::comm::TNOTIFY(v41, v12, v11);               // cross-rank signal races the in-flight stores
...
pto::comm::TWAIT(v44, v12, v10);                 // peer unblocks and reads partial data
```

PTOAS emits only the local `set_flag(PIPE_MTE3, PIPE_MTE2, ...)` after `TPUT`; there is no `pipe_barrier(PIPE_ALL)` (or equivalent MTE3 drain) between the chunked `TPUT` and the following `TNOTIFY`.

## Expected

A chunked `pto::comm::TPUT` followed by a visibility/signal op (`TNOTIFY`) must guarantee all chunk stores have landed before the signal fires — same effective completion guarantee as single-shot TPUT. Either:

1. **insert-sync** should emit a full `pipe_barrier(PIPE_ALL)` (or MTE3 drain) between a chunked `pto.comm.tput` and a following `pto.system.notify` / `pto.comm.tnotify`; or
2. the **chunked TPUT** implementation should be self-completing (drain its last chunk before returning), matching single-shot semantics.

## Workaround (verified)

Inserting a `pipe_barrier(PIPE_ALL)` immediately after `TPUT` (before `TNOTIFY`) makes the chunked case correct on device. We currently inject this from the PyPTO frontend codegen as a stopgap, but it should be PTOAS's responsibility (single-shot TPUT needs no such caller-inserted barrier).

## Environment

- Platform: a2a3 (Ascend 910B), 2 ranks
- pto-isa commit: `016396b57e2c17093f1194e6acd89bb112b0ab24`
- Frontend: PyPTO `pld.tensor.put` with sub-tile VEC staging (auto-chunk)

## Related

- #706 — [Pass Bug] insert-sync: missing MTE3->MTE2 hazard between `pto.tstore` and `pto.comm.tput`
- #730 — [Bug] insert-sync: MTE3->MTE2 pipe flag for same-address GM store->load round-trip doesn't guarantee GM visibility

title: [Bug] tload template failed for qwen3 cube kernel
body:
### Component

PTO Dialect / ODS (include/PTO/IR)

### Description

`lib/TileOps/tload_template.py` 有两个 Cube 路径的 `tload` 模板（`ND2NZ` 和 `DN2NZ`），当源 view 的 `valid_shape` 为动态（`v_row=?` / `v_col=?`）时，两个 constraint 都返回 `True`，导致 `select_kernel()` 报二义性错误。

另外，缺少 `DN2ZN`（DN → transposed NZ，`blayout=row_major, slayout=col_major`）模板，导致 QK matmul（`incore_4`）的 K^T 加载失败。该模式在 `pto-isa` 的 C++ ISA 中已实现（`TLoad.hpp:472, TLoadCubeDN2ZN`），硬件通过复用 `nd2nz` 指令 + 行列参数互换来完成，不需要新的硬件指令。

### Reproduction (minimal)

```markdown
cd test/samples/Qwen3DecodeA5

# Cube kernel (tload 二义性)
ptoas qwen3_decode_incore_1.pto --pto-arch=a5 --pto-backend=vpto --pto-level=level3 -o /tmp/test.o
# Error: select_kernel() found multiple highest-priority kernels for tload:
#   tload_gm_to_mat_dn2nz (priority=1) vs tload_gm_to_mat_nd2nz (priority=1)

# QK matmul (缺失 DN2ZN 模板)
ptoas qwen3_decode_incore_4.pto --pto-arch=a5 --pto-backend=vpto --pto-level=level3 -o /tmp/test.o
# Error: select_kernel() found no registered kernel after constraint evaluation for tload
```

### Expected behavior

- 当 `valid_shape` 为动态时，通过源 view 的 `layout` 属性（`#pto.layout<nd>` / `#pto.layout<dn>`）来消歧，正确匹配 `ND2NZ` 或 `DN2NZ` 模板。
- DM→transposed NZ（`blayout=row_major, slayout=col_major`）的 Cube 加载应匹配 `DN2ZN` 模板。

### Actual behavior / error logs

```text
Qwen3DecodeA5 的所有 Cube kernel 在 VPTO 路径下编译均失败：

| Kernel | 错误 |
|--------|------|
| incore_1/2/6/10/11 | `multiple highest-priority kernels ... tload_gm_to_mat_dn2nz vs tload_gm_to_mat_nd2nz` |
| incore_4 | `no registered kernel after constraint evaluation for tload` |

根因分析：

1. **ND2NZ/DN2NZ 二义性**：两个 constraint 都要求 `dst.blayout=COL_MAJOR, dst.slayout=ROW_MAJOR`，当 `valid_shape=[null, null]` 时，`_known_eq()` 遇 `None` 返回 `True`，两个 constraint 同时通过，`select_kernel()` 报二义性。

2. **DN2ZN 缺失**：incore_4 的 K tile 需要 `blayout=ROW_MAJOR, slayout=COL_MAJOR`（转置 NZ），不匹配任何现有模板。硬件 C++ ISA 已支持（`TLoadCubeDN2ZN`），它内部复用 `nd2nz` 硬件指令 + 行列参数互换，但 TileOps 模板库缺少对应封装。
```

title: 0.47 regression: `func.func private` lowered without `static` (external linkage) → duplicate-symbol collisions, AICORE_EXCEPTION 507015
body:
## Summary

Starting in **ptoas 0.47**, a `func.func private` (internal-linkage) function is
lowered to C++ **without the `static` qualifier**, giving it *external* linkage.
0.45 and 0.46 correctly emit it as `static`.

When two kernels that each carry a private helper of the **same name** (a common
pattern for the distributed comm helpers `CommRemoteOffset_i32` / `_bf16` /
`_i8` / `_f32`, which PyPTO emits into every comm kernel) are compiled to
separate `.o` and linked into one device program, the now-external symbols
**collide (ODR / duplicate definition)**. The linked kernel is corrupted and
faults at runtime with `ACL_ERROR_RT_AICORE_EXCEPTION (507015)`.

## Impact

PyPTO DeepSeek-V4 distributed MoE (`--ep 2`, two ranks) compiles and runs
cleanly with ptoas 0.45/0.46, but with 0.47 it crashes on device during stream
sync:

```
[ERROR] sync_run_streams: aclrtSynchronizeStreamWithTimeout (AICPU) failed: 507015
[ERROR] AICore error 507015: bounded device drain failed: 507015
```

Both `combine_push` and `dispatch` (linked together) define
`func.func private @CommRemoteOffset_i32`. Under 0.47 each `.o` exports it as a
**global** symbol:

```
# nm combine_push.o   (ptoas 0.47)
0000000000000000 T _Z20CommRemoteOffset_i32PU3AS1ll      <- global, should be local
# nm dispatch.o       (ptoas 0.47)
000000000000002c T _Z20CommRemoteOffset_i32PU3AS1ll      <- duplicate global
```

Under 0.45/0.46 the same symbol is `static` (file-local), no collision.

## Minimal reproducer

`repro.pto`:

```mlir
module {
  func.func @k(%arg0: !pto.ptr<i64>, %arg1: index) attributes {pto.kernel_kind = #pto.kernel_kind<vector>} {
    %0 = func.call @my_helper(%arg1) : (index) -> index
    func.return
  }
  func.func private @my_helper(%x: index) -> index {
    %c = arith.constant 1 : index
    %r = arith.addi %x, %c : index
    return %r : index
  }
}
```

```
ptoas repro.pto -o repro.cpp --enable-insert-sync --pto-level=level3 --pto-arch a3
grep my_helper repro.cpp
```

| ptoas | output for the `private` helper |
| ----- | ------------------------------- |
| 0.45  | `static AICORE int64_t my_helper(int64_t v1) {`  ✅ |
| 0.46  | `static AICORE int64_t my_helper(int64_t v1) {`  ✅ |
| 0.47  | `AICORE int64_t my_helper(int64_t v1) {`  ❌ (missing `static`) |

## Expected vs actual

- **Expected:** `func.func private @foo` lowers to an internal-linkage C++
  definition (`static ...`), as in 0.45/0.46.
- **Actual (0.47):** the `private` symbol visibility is ignored and the function
  is emitted with external linkage, causing duplicate-symbol collisions when
  multiple kernels carry same-named private helpers.

## Notes

The faulty entry-point handling around the same area also changed in 0.47
(0.45 emitted `extern "C" __global__ AICORE void <kernel>(...)`, 0.47 emits
plain `AICORE void <kernel>(...)`), but PyPTO normalizes the entry qualifier, so
that part is harmless. The **dropped `static` on `private` functions** is the
regression that breaks linking. A fix that re-honors MLIR `sym_visibility =
"private"` (→ `static`) restores correct behavior.

Environment: aarch64, CANN 9.0.0, `--pto-arch a3` (Ascend 910B). The missing
`static` reproduces independently of `--pto-arch` and `--enable-insert-sync`.

title: [Feature] Add optional PTODSL launch profile object to measure kernel runtime without compile/build overhead
body:
## Summary

PTODSL currently mixes compilation/build work into the launch path, which makes it hard to measure kernel execution time accurately from Python.

I would like PTODSL launch to accept an optional `profile` object. When this object is provided, the generated launch path should insert profiling/statistics code immediately around the real kernel invocation, so that after launch finishes we can read kernel performance data from `profile` without counting PTODSL tracing / PTOAS / Bisheng build overhead.

## Motivation / use case

Today, the first PTODSL launch may include both:

- JIT specialization/tracing on the `kernel[grid, stream]` path
- Native build / shared-library generation on the first actual call path

From the current code:

- `KernelHandle.__getitem__()` calls `self.compile()` before returning the launch handle (`ptodsl/ptodsl/_jit.py`, lines 294-297)
- `KernelCompiler.compile()` may trace and `compiled.build()` a new specialization when it is not cached (`ptodsl/ptodsl/_kernel_compilation.py`, lines 81-119)
- `LaunchHandle._ensure_launch_fn()` lazily calls `build_native_library()` on first launch (`ptodsl/ptodsl/_runtime/launch.py`, lines 134-149)
- `build_native_library()` may run `ptoas`, Bisheng compile, and link steps when the native cache is cold (`ptodsl/ptodsl/_runtime/native_build.py`, lines 178-233)

Because some of this work happens on the launch path, it is difficult to use PTODSL itself to answer a simple question: how long did the kernel actually run?

In practice, users can manually warm up with `.compile()` and extra launches, but that is easy to forget, is not ergonomic, and still does not provide a standard PTODSL-side profiling interface.

## Proposed API / behavior

Suggested direction:

```python
profile = pto.LaunchProfile()
compiled[grid, stream](arg0, arg1, ..., profile=profile)
# or: kernel[grid, stream](..., profile=profile)
```

When `profile` is present:

- PTODSL should keep the existing compile/cache behavior unchanged
- The generated launch code should insert timing/stat collection immediately before and after the real kernel invocation point
- The measured result should reflect kernel runtime as closely as possible, rather than Python-side tracing / compilation / native build overhead
- The collected data should be readable from the `profile` object after launch completes

Possible data fields could include:

- kernel elapsed time
- launch timestamp / end timestamp
- optional cache-hit or compile/build metadata as separate fields, if that is useful

Backward compatibility:

- No behavior change when `profile` is omitted
- Existing launch syntax should keep working

## Alternatives considered

- Ask users to always call `.compile()` manually and then do multiple warm-up launches before measuring
- Add a separate explicit `prepare()` / `build()` API and require users to split preparation from measurement themselves

Those approaches help, but they still leave PTODSL without a built-in, user-facing profiling surface attached to launch itself.

## Additional context

The key point is not only “add profiling”, but “profile around the real kernel call site”. Otherwise the reported numbers will still be polluted by first-launch compilation/build work and will be hard to compare across kernels.

title: level2 PlanMemory: how to express in-place / loop-carried tile buffer reuse (aliasing without addr)?
body:
## Summary

At `--pto-level=level2` (PlanMemory owns allocation), what is the **canonical / supported way to express that two `pto.alloc_tile` results must resolve to the same physical buffer** — i.e. in-place reuse across a loop (loop-carried accumulator) or in-place ops?

We (PyPTO) are adding a mode that stops baking physical addresses and hands allocation to PlanMemory (`level2`). It works for kernels without buffer aliasing, but **silently miscompiles loop-carried tile accumulators**, and we can't find the right level2 IR to express the aliasing.

## Background

Today PyPTO runs at `level3`: it assigns addresses itself and encodes "these two tiles are the same buffer" purely by giving two separate `pto.alloc_tile` ops the **same `addr`**. At `level2` there is no `addr`, and PlanMemory allocates each `alloc_tile` independently — so the aliasing is lost.

## Minimal repro

A loop-carried accumulator (`acc = acc + t` each iteration). At level2 the `.pto` is:

```mlir
module attributes {pto.target_arch = "a2a3"} {
  func.func @kernel(%arg0: !pto.ptr<f32>, %arg1: !pto.ptr<f32>, %arg2: index) attributes {pto.kernel_kind = #pto.kernel_kind<vector>} {
  %c128_index = arith.constant 128 : index
  %c64_index = arith.constant 64 : index
  %c1_index = arith.constant 1 : index
  %c0_index = arith.constant 0 : index
  %a_view = pto.make_tensor_view %arg0, shape = [%c128_index, %c64_index], strides = [%c64_index, %c1_index] {layout = #pto.layout<nd>}: !pto.tensor_view<?x?xf32>
  %out_view = pto.make_tensor_view %arg1, shape = [%c64_index, %c64_index], strides = [%c64_index, %c1_index] {layout = #pto.layout<nd>}: !pto.tensor_view<?x?xf32>
  %acc = pto.alloc_tile valid_row = %c64_index valid_col = %c64_index : !pto.tile_buf<loc=vec, dtype=f32, rows=64, cols=64, v_row=?, v_col=?, blayout=row_major, slayout=none_box, fractal=512, pad=0>
  %a_pview = pto.partition_view %a_view, offsets = [%c0_index, %c0_index], sizes = [%c64_index, %c64_index] : !pto.tensor_view<?x?xf32> -> !pto.partition_tensor_view<64x64xf32>
  pto.tload ins(%a_pview : !pto.partition_tensor_view<64x64xf32>) outs(%acc : !pto.tile_buf<loc=vec, dtype=f32, rows=64, cols=64, v_row=?, v_col=?, blayout=row_major, slayout=none_box, fractal=512, pad=0>)
  scf.for %i = %c0_index to %arg2 step %c1_index {
    %t = pto.alloc_tile valid_row = %c64_index valid_col = %c64_index : !pto.tile_buf<loc=vec, dtype=f32, rows=64, cols=64, v_row=?, v_col=?, blayout=row_major, slayout=none_box, fractal=512, pad=0>
    %0 = arith.muli %i, %c64_index : index
    %1 = pto.partition_view %a_view, offsets = [%0, %c0_index], sizes = [%c64_index, %c64_index] : !pto.tensor_view<?x?xf32> -> !pto.partition_tensor_view<64x64xf32>
    pto.tload ins(%1 : !pto.partition_tensor_view<64x64xf32>) outs(%t : !pto.tile_buf<loc=vec, dtype=f32, rows=64, cols=64, v_row=?, v_col=?, blayout=row_major, slayout=none_box, fractal=512, pad=0>)
    %acc_next = pto.alloc_tile valid_row = %c64_index valid_col = %c64_index : !pto.tile_buf<loc=vec, dtype=f32, rows=64, cols=64, v_row=?, v_col=?, blayout=row_major, slayout=none_box, fractal=512, pad=0>
    pto.tadd ins(%acc, %t : !pto.tile_buf<...>, !pto.tile_buf<...>) outs(%acc_next : !pto.tile_buf<...>)
  }
  %out_pview = pto.partition_view %out_view, offsets = [%c0_index, %c0_index], sizes = [%c64_index, %c64_index] : !pto.tensor_view<?x?xf32> -> !pto.partition_tensor_view<64x64xf32>
  pto.tstore ins(%acc : !pto.tile_buf<...>) outs(%out_pview : !pto.partition_tensor_view<64x64xf32>)
  return
  }
}
```

Compiled with:

```
ptoas repro.pto -o repro.cce --enable-insert-sync --pto-level=level2 --pto-arch a3
```

(ptoas **0.48**)

## Observed vs expected

**level2 output (wrong)** — PlanMemory gives `acc` and `acc_next` **different** addresses, so the accumulation writes to a scratch buffer and the store reads the pre-loop value:

```cpp
TASSIGN(v9,  0);       // acc      @ 0
TASSIGN(v15, 16384);   // t        @ 16384
TASSIGN(v20, 32768);   // acc_next @ 32768   <-- different buffer from acc
TADD(v20, v9, v15);    // acc_next = acc + t   (acc never updated)
...
TSTORE(v24, v9);       // stores acc @ 0 == initial load, accumulation lost
```

**level3 output (correct)** — same kernel with `addr` baked; `acc` and `acc_next` get the **same** address, so it accumulates in place:

```cpp
TASSIGN(v8,  0);       // acc      @ 0
TASSIGN(v19, 0);       // acc_next @ 0        <-- same buffer as acc
TADD(v19, v8, v14);    // in-place: acc = acc + t
TSTORE(v23, v8);       // stores accumulated result
```

## Root cause / the gap

Read purely as SSA dataflow, the level2 `.pto` above is already "wrong": the `scf.for` has **empty iter_args**, `%acc_next` is never fed back as `%acc`, and the store reads the pre-loop `%acc`. In level3 the only thing that made it correct was the shared `addr` side-channel. So we need a **structural** way to express the in-place / loop-carried buffer reuse that PlanMemory honors.

## Question

What is the expected/supported level2 encoding for "these tile buffers must be the same allocation"? Candidates we considered — which (if any) does PlanMemory honor, and is there a canonical one?

1. **`scf.for` iter_args carrying the `!pto.tile_buf` value** — yield `%acc_next` and re-bind it as `%acc` for the next iteration, so the carried buffer is a real loop-carried SSA value. (Does PlanMemory allocate one buffer for a tile-typed iter_arg + its yielded value?)
2. **Reuse a single `alloc_tile` / in-place op form** — write the result into the same `%acc` SSA (an in-place `tadd` whose out aliases an in operand) instead of allocating `%acc_next`.
3. **An explicit alias/in-place attribute or op** on the alloc or the op that tells PlanMemory to co-locate two allocations.

Could you point us at the recommended pattern (ideally a tiny before/after `.pto`) for:
- loop-carried tile accumulators,
- and in-place elementwise ops (`out` aliases an `in`)?

That lets us emit the correct level2 IR from PyPTO instead of relying on identical `addr`. Thanks!

title: [Bug] SPMD loop-carried scalar accumulator read after the loop is wrong on ~half the blocks (correct .pto/.cpp)
body:
## Background

In pypto-lib, a `pl.spmd` block that builds a per-block value with a **loop-carried scalar accumulator** and reads it **after** the loop miscompiles: on device ~5-8 of 16 SPMD blocks write the accumulator's **initial value (0)** instead of the accumulated sum. The `.pto` handed to ptoas and the ptoas-generated `.cpp` are both correct, so the defect is in ptoas's AIV lowering / per-block scalar GM-store write-back.

This is the root cause of a dsv4 MoE failure (`models/deepseek/v4/moe.py`, `-p a2a3 --ep 2`): folding the dispatch cumsum into the SPMD gather makes `recv_count_out` (= final acc) wrong on ~half the experts, so `expert_routed` reads a stale/0 count as its dynamic loop bound -> `x_next` golden fails ~71%.

Reproduce (single card):

    task-submit --device auto --device-num 1 --run "python repro_spmd_loopcarry_count.py -p a2a3"

Symptom class: **precision** (wrong output, no crash). Intermittent: the *number* of wrong blocks varies run-to-run (e.g. 8/16 then 5/16), but some blocks always fail.

Reproduction environment:

| Component | Version |
|---|---|
| pypto-lib | `ece27f8` (branch: `dsv4-moe-parallel-gather`) |
| pypto | `a028dcb4` (branch: `main`) |
| simpler | `fb65fe9d` (detached) |
| ptoas | `0.48` |
| pto-isa | `016396b5` |
| CANN | not detected |

Version note: pto-isa is off its pin (expected `83d01313...`, actual `016396b5`). Irrelevant here -- the reproducer is a pure scalar loop with **zero tile-ISA ops**, and the diagnosed component **ptoas 0.48 matches its pin (`v0.48`)**.

Diagnosis: **ptoas** -- the `.pto` input and the ptoas-generated `.cpp` both correctly thread the loop-carried accumulator; only the runtime result is wrong, on a subset of SPMD blocks.

Related: PTOAS#696 (closed -- "Missing dcci+dsb after scalar GM stores causes cross-AICore data races"), PTOAS#872 (open -- stores not drained before TNOTIFY), pypto-lib#419.

### Minimal reproducer

The kernel (full standalone script `repro_spmd_loopcarry_count.py` below):

```python
N = 16   # SPMD blocks
K = 4    # lanes summed per block
UNIT = 8 # each lane contributes UNIT

@pl.jit
def repro(cnt: pl.Tensor[[N, K], pl.INT32],
          count_out: pl.Out[pl.Tensor[[N, 1], pl.INT32]]):
    with pl.spmd(N, name_hint="count_spmd") as _tid:
        e = pl.tile.get_block_idx()
        acc = pl.const(0, pl.INT32)
        for src in pl.range(K):
            acc = acc + pl.read(cnt, [e, src])   # loop-carried accumulation
        pl.write(count_out, [e, 0], acc)         # read final acc AFTER the loop
    return count_out
```

`cnt` is all-`UNIT`, so every `count_out[e]` should be `K*UNIT = 32`. Device result: ~5-8 of 16 entries are `0`.

### IR evidence (ptoas input + output both correct)

`ptoas/count.pto` (input to ptoas) -- loop-carry is correct:

```mlir
%acc_rv = scf.for %src = %c0 to %c4 step %c1 iter_args(%acc = %c0_i32) -> (i32) {
  %t = pto.load_scalar %arg0[%off] : !pto.ptr<i32> -> i32
  %0 = arith.addi %acc, %t : i32
  scf.yield %0 : i32
}
pto.store_scalar %acc_rv, %arg1[%e] : !pto.ptr<i32>, i32
```

`ptoas/count.cpp` (ptoas-generated) -- textbook-correct:

```cpp
int32_t v10;  v10 = 0;                 // acc init
for (int64_t v11 = 0; v11 < 4; v11 += 1) {
  int32_t v12 = cnt[e*4 + v11];
  uint32_t v13 = (uint32_t) v10;
  v10 = (int32_t)(v13 + (uint32_t) v12);   // acc += cnt
}
int32_t v14 = v10;
count_out[e] = v14;                    // store final acc
```

Correct C++, wrong runtime result on ~half the blocks -> the defect is **below** the generated C++ (AIV machine-code generation, or the per-block scalar GM store write-back / cache flush -- cf. the closed PTOAS#696).

### Notes
- Standalone variants where the loop-carried value is used as a `pl.load`/`pl.store` offset *inside* the loop all pass golden -- the failure is specifically the **post-loop read** of the accumulator (its final store per block).
- Workaround in pypto-lib: compute the accumulation in an AICPU `pl.at(CORE_GROUP)` task and pass results into the SPMD region as plain tensors (avoids the SPMD post-loop scalar store).

### Full reproducer script

```python
import pypto.language as pl

N = 16       # SPMD blocks
K = 4        # lanes summed per block
UNIT = 8     # each lane contributes UNIT


@pl.jit
def repro(
    cnt: pl.Tensor[[N, K], pl.INT32],
    count_out: pl.Out[pl.Tensor[[N, 1], pl.INT32]],
):
    with pl.spmd(N, name_hint="count_spmd") as _tid:
        e = pl.tile.get_block_idx()
        acc = pl.const(0, pl.INT32)
        for src in pl.range(K):
            acc = acc + pl.read(cnt, [e, src])
        pl.write(count_out, [e, 0], acc)
    return count_out


def build_specs():
    import torch
    from golden import TensorSpec
    return [
        TensorSpec("cnt", [N, K], torch.int32, init_value=UNIT),
        TensorSpec("count_out", [N, 1], torch.int32, is_output=True, init_value=0),
    ]


def golden_repro(values):
    cnt = values["cnt"]
    count_out = values["count_out"]
    for e in range(N):
        count_out[e, 0] = int(cnt[e].sum().item())   # == K * UNIT == 32


if __name__ == "__main__":
    import argparse
    from golden import run_jit
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("-p", "--platform", type=str, default="a2a3")
    parser.add_argument("-d", "--device", type=int, default=0)
    parser.add_argument("--compile-only", action="store_true", default=False)
    parser.add_argument("--dump-passes", action="store_true", default=False)
    args = parser.parse_args()
    result = run_jit(
        fn=repro, specs=build_specs(), golden_fn=golden_repro,
        compile_only=args.compile_only,
        compile_cfg=dict(dump_passes=args.dump_passes),
        runtime_cfg=dict(platform=args.platform, device_id=args.device),
        rtol=0, atol=0,
    )
    if not result.passed:
        if result.error:
            print(result.error)
        raise SystemExit(1)
```

title: [Bug] False-positive ast_rewrite runtime loop IV exposure for sibling range(...) loops reusing 'c'
body:
### Component
Other (`ptodsl/ptodsl/_ast_rewrite.py` AST rewrite frontend)

### Description
`ast_rewrite=True` appears to raise a false positive for runtime `range(...)` loops when sibling runtime loops reuse the same induction variable name.

In the reproducer below, the first `for c in range(cols):` does not intentionally use `c` after the loop exits, but `probe.compile()` still fails with:

```text
ptodsl._ast_rewrite.PTODSLAstRewriteError: ast_rewrite=True runtime for-loops cannot expose the loop induction variable outside the loop yet; use explicit pto.for_(...) for 'c'
```

A practical workaround on my side is to rename the later sibling runtime loop variables (`c` -> `dpost_chunk`, `dcomb_chunk`, etc.). After renaming, the same kernel shape compiles.

So this looks like a frontend liveness / loop-IV analysis issue rather than a real user-side use-after-loop of the induction variable.

### Reproduction (minimal)
`repro.py`

```python
from ptodsl import pto

@pto.jit(target="a5")
def probe(rows: pto.i32, cols: pto.i32):
    mask1 = 1
    mask_all = 2
    for t in range(rows):
        for c in range(cols):
            col = c * 64
            mask = col
            d_heads = [mask + h for h in pto.static_range(4)]
            acc = None
            for h in pto.static_range(4):
                term = d_heads[h]
                acc = term if acc is None else acc + term
            sink = acc + col + mask

        for mo in pto.static_range(4):
            mix_acc = 0
            for c in range(cols):
                col = c * 64
                mask = col
                mix_acc = mix_acc + mask
            sum_v = mix_acc + mask_all
            out = sum_v + mask1

print(probe.compile().mlir_text())
```

Run:

```bash
python repro.py
```

Notes:
- If I rename the second loop variable from `c` to something else, the error goes away.
- I reduced this from a larger VMI kernel where several sibling `for c in range(chunks):` loops lived under the same outer `for t in range(num_tokens):` block.

### Expected behavior
The frontend should accept this pattern, or at least not report that `c` is exposed outside the loop when it is only reused as the induction variable of a later sibling runtime loop.

### Actual behavior / error logs
```text
Traceback (most recent call last):
  ...
  File "/home/zhangzhendong/ptoas-workspace/PTOAS/ptodsl/ptodsl/_ast_rewrite.py", line 634, in _rewrite_for
    raise PTODSLAstRewriteError(
ptodsl._ast_rewrite.PTODSLAstRewriteError: ast_rewrite=True runtime for-loops cannot expose the loop induction variable outside the loop yet; use explicit pto.for_(...) for 'c'
```

title: [Bug] PlanMemory (level2) reuses a live tile's UB range for a row_sum tmp without a store→vector sync → data race corrupts the output
body:
## Background

In pypto-lib, `tests/st/codegen/dsl/repro_qk_norm_race.py` on `a2a3` has a **precision**
problem under `memory_planner=PtoAS` (`--pto-level=level2`): a Qwen3-style QK-norm kernel's
k-half `col_expand_mul` output (`k_proj_norm`) comes out wrong (max|err|≈25, 1902/2048
elements), while the structurally identical q-half is correct — a clean **q-PASS / k-FAIL**
signature. It compiles and runs; only the numbers are wrong. The default PyPTO planner passes.

Reproduce with:

    python tests/st/codegen/dsl/repro_qk_norm_race.py -d 1              # PtoAS -> k_g FAIL
    python tests/st/codegen/dsl/repro_qk_norm_race.py -d 1 --baseline   # PyPTO -> all PASS

Reproduction environment:

| Component | Version |
|---|---|
| pypto-lib | `d998b8b` (branch: `qwen3-14b/drop-dead-hidden-states-arg`) |
| pypto | `de953d10` (branch: `test/ptoas-matmul-kreduction-st`) |
| simpler | `c94aa9f3` (detached) |
| ptoas | `0.48` |
| pto-isa | `016396b5` |
| CANN | `9.0.0` |

Version mismatch (off pinned): pto-isa expected `83d01313`, actual `016396b5`. Not relevant to
this fault — the defect is visible directly in ptoas's emitted `.cpp` (instruction stream +
UB addresses), independent of the pto-isa tile-op implementation.

Diagnosis: **ptoas** — its PlanMemory (level2) both reuses a still-live output buffer's UB
range for a `row_sum` tmp workspace AND omits the store→vector sync it correctly inserts on
the sibling q-half.

Related: pypto-lib#713 (same k-half QK-output corruption symptom, not yet traced to ptoas).

### Root cause

The kernel does, for each of q and k, in one CORE_GROUP scope:

```
chunk = row_expand_mul(proj_slice, inv_rms_col)   # [.,128]
g     = col_expand_mul(chunk, gamma)              # [.,128]  -> tstore  (this is *_proj_norm)
inv   = recip(sqrt(row_sum(chunk*chunk)/D + eps)) # row_sum uses a tmp workspace tile
```

The level2 `.pto` is addr-less and semantically correct (an isolated program with the same
math compiles fine). Both `g` (col_expand output) and the `row_sum` tmp are plain addr-less
`alloc_tile`s; ptoas assigns their UB addresses and inserts sync. In the k-half it does two
things wrong:

**1. Overlapping UB reuse.** `g` (k_g) is DEAD after its `tstore`, so reusing its address for
the tmp is legal — but ptoas places the tmp *inside* k_g's still-in-flight range:

```
k_norm_w  @ 768    [768,  1280)
k_g       @ 1280   [1280, 9472)   <- col_expand output, being stored (MTE3)
k tmp     @ 8192   [8192, 8256)   <- row_sum tmp: INSIDE k_g's range
k_chunk   @ 9472   [9472, ...)
```

**2. Missing store→vector sync.** After k_g's async `TSTORE` (MTE3) it goes straight to the
vector `TMUL`/`TROWSUM` (which writes the tmp @8192) with **no** `set_flag/wait_flag(PIPE_MTE3,
PIPE_V)`. So the vector tmp write races the not-yet-finished k_g store into overlapping UB and
corrupts k_g.

The q-half (identical shape) is compiled correctly — its tmp lands outside q_g **and** it emits
the MTE3→V handshake — proving the fault is ptoas-side and half-specific. `k_inv` is also
correct, because `row_sum`'s dst and src (k_chunk) are outside the clobbered range; only k_g is
hit.

### The smoking gun (ptoas-emitted `.cpp`)

```c
// q-half  (CORRECT)                          // k-half  (BUGGY)
TCOLEXPANDMUL(v50, v49, v32)  // q_g          TCOLEXPANDMUL(v82, v80, v37)  // k_g
set_flag (PIPE_V,   PIPE_MTE3)                set_flag (PIPE_V,   PIPE_MTE3)
wait_flag(PIPE_V,   PIPE_MTE3)                wait_flag(PIPE_V,   PIPE_MTE3)
TSTORE(v55, v52)              // q_g store    TSTORE(v86, v82)              // k_g store (MTE3)
set_flag (PIPE_MTE3, PIPE_V)  // <-- store->  // <-- MISSING set_flag/wait_flag(MTE3,V)
wait_flag(PIPE_MTE3, PIPE_V)  //     vector   TMUL(v87, v80, v80)          // races the store
TMUL(v56, v49, v49)                           TROWSUM(v91, v87, v89)       // tmp @8192 in k_g
TROWSUM(v60, v56, v58)        // tmp @42240   ...
                             // (outside q_g) wait_flag(PIPE_MTE3, PIPE_V) // too late (after)
```

### Attached files

- `repro_qk_norm_race.py` — standalone device repro (q-PASS / k-FAIL)
- `qk_norm.level2.pto` — the addr-less level2 IR ptoas is fed
- `qk_norm.cce.cpp` — ptoas's emitted `.cpp` (the overlap + missing sync are visible here)

(Trigger detail: gamma must be a scope-external `slice` of a weight tensor, as in decode_layer's
`k_norm_w = slice(k_norm_weight, [1,D], [layer,0])`; a bare `[1,D]` arg gets a non-overlapping
layout and passes.)
